articles.title: U.S. federal court strikes down fixed terms for student, exchange visas
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: In July, the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) proposed a policy aimed at preventing international students from staying in the country for more than four years unless they obtained federal approval
A U.S. federal court has struck down a Trump administration proposal to cap the amount of time foreign students, scholars, and journalists can spend in the country on their respective visas.

In July, the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) proposed a policy aimed at preventing international students from staying in the country for more than four years unless they obtained federal approval.

Boston federal Judge F. Dennis Saylor delivered a ruling on Monday (November 16, 2026) striking down the DHS proposal as "arbitrary, capricious, an abuse of discretion, and otherwise not in accordance with law."

"Put bluntly, DHS is seeking to prevent or discourage the very activity — providing educational opportunities for foreign students in the United States — that Congress sought to permit and encourage," Judge Saylor said in his ruling.
"The statute simply does not grant DHS such broad and open-ended authority to undermine the F-1 visa programme," he added.
The proposed rule also sought to shorten how long foreign journalists can stay in the country from several years to 240 days – or 90 days for Chinese journalists.
The proposed rule also shortened the grace period – the window to depart after finishing studies or post-completion OPT from 60 days to 30.
For language programmes, there was an aggregate limit of 24 months for stays, including breaks and vacations.
The Foundation for India and Indian Diaspora Studies (FIIDS) welcomed the federal court order.

"Once again, the court has come to the rescue of international students — and, in doing so, has helped protect the future of American science, technology, research, and innovation," said FIIDS President and Chief of Policy and Strategy, Khanderao Kand.

Miriam Feldblum, president and CEO of the Presidents' Alliance on Higher Education and Education, one of the lead plaintiffs, termed the federal court ruling as a clear and important victory for international students and scholars and the colleges and universities that welcome them.

"The harmful consequences of the current administration's policy actions and efforts are already evident in the significant declines in international student enrolment and interest we are witnessing," Ms. Feldblum said in a statement.

articles.title: Dengue spurt in Thiruvananthapuram: KU’s Karyavattom campus, Cliff House compound emerge as hotspots
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Intermittent spells of rain, followed by hot and humid weather, have led to a spike in dengue cases in Thiruvananthapuram, even as the overall trend in dengue cases across the State has been on a slow decline since July

The Karyavattom campus of Kerala University (KU) has emerged as a hotspot of dengue in the city, where over 50 cases have been reported since November 9. Health department suspects that this is a gross underestimation, as the transmission is likely to have begun weeks before

Intermittent spells of rain, followed by hot and humid weather, have led to the spike in dengue cases in Thiruvananthapuram, even when the general dengue case trend has been on a slow decline since July across the State.
In the last 10 days, Thiruvananthapuram district has reported 200 probable cases of dengue and 97 confirmed cases.

On Monday, following a meeting called by the Health department, which was joined by the Vice Chancellor, some KU syndicate members as well as public health experts of the School of Public Health under Kerala University of Health Sciences, it was decided to shut the Karyavattom campus and the hostel buildings for three days so that intense vector control measures can be taken up and a break in disease transmission can be achieved.

“District health officials and vector control teams had visited the campus and hostel and we found that solid waste management was a huge issue in the campus. Plastic disposable containers used for food delivery which are disposed of carelessly are emerging as a major contributor to vector breeding in urban areas.. Rain water stagnation in these containers which are strewn around is a major hazard. Indoor plants in hostel rooms, broken manholes and blocked drains leading to rainwater stagnation have all led to intense mosquito breeding inside the vast campus,” a senior Health official said.

The Health department has also decided to serve notice to the KU Registrar under the Kerala Public Health Act, for allowing the campus to be a breeding ground for mosquitoes and posing a public health issue

Teams from the Pangappara health centre have been at work on the campus since November 10 but the district vector control team and the Corporation health staff will be joining them now. Fogging will be done to kill adult mosquitoes and indoor space spraying inside the hostel room, which will be accompanied by a source reduction campaign, officials said.
The district health administration has identified several pockets of dengue within the city itself, where an abundance of breeding sources and intense vector breeding has been spotted
Health officials point out that several large government properties with vast, ill-maintained grounds are also turning out to be hotspots for dengue in the city.

“The Cliff House compound and the sprawling official bungalows around it are all major breeding grounds for mosquitoes. In the Cliff House, seven police personnel there on guard duty were down with dengue, following which a district health team had visited the location. In some of the bungalows where renovation works are going on, building materials and discarded parts of equipment are all thrown about carelessly, leading to rain water stagnation and mosquito breeding,” a health official said.
Health officials said that without public participation, source reduction and mosquito control cannot be taken up successfully.
Kollam district too has reported a significant number of dengue cases over the last 10 days.

fullParagraphs: The Tamil Nadu Medical Officers Association (TNMOA) has urged the Chief Minister, Health Minister and Managing Director of Tamil Nadu Medical Services (TNMSC) to cancel the corporation’s recent tenders to carry out repair works at warehouses of Tamil Nadu State Marketing Corporation (TASMAC) and to direct that the works be undertaken through the Public Works Department or another agency.

When TNMSC was earlier made to procure gold coins (for ‘Thaimaaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam’ ), it drew strong criticism. Now, using TNMSC to take up repair works at TASMAC warehouses is strongly condemnable, TNMOA said in a statement.
Symbolism or substance? Tamil Nadu’s public health professionals question gold ring scheme

Earlier, The Hindu had reported that TNMSC has invited tenders for special repairs at TASMAC warehouses in three locations.

TNMSC was established to procure quality medical equipment and medicines at affordable cost for the Health department, it said. The association said that already, several irregularities were reported in TNMSC’s core function of procuring medicines. There were repeated instances of TNMSC issuing ‘No Objection Certificates’ instead of procuring essential medicines and asking college deans and joint directors to purchase them using funds under the Chief Minister’s Comprehensive Health Insurance Scheme (CMCHIS).

The association expressed concern that instead of addressing the shortcomings and strengthening TNMSC, a model agency in the country, the State government is taking steps that undermine the institution.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Does Indian law require Microsoft to have reported the recent outage that affected customers’ ability to access its productivity suite? What rules apply in such situations and what are their shortcomings in the present form? How are cloud companies accountable in other countries? What are Indian customers’ options?

From November 12 to 13, an as-yet unspecified problem with Microsoft infrastructure affected customers’ ability to access its productivity suite Microsoft 365 worldwide, including its Outlook email service. Microsoft apologised during the outage and attributed the incident to a fault in an upgrade of its network capacity, although more precise details are still expected.
In India, among consequences in various sectors, IndiGo and Akasa Air alerted passengers of disruptions to their email support while Air India rerouted its email.

articles.title: Air purifier sales surge as demand, smart features drive market growth
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: While Delhi-NCR remains the dominant market, cities like Mumbai and regions beyond traditional high-pollution belts are showing sustained upticks

Demand for air purifiers in India has witnessed explosive growth in 2026, with major brands and retail platforms reporting sales doubling or tripling year-on-year. Driven by an early surge ahead of the traditional winter pollution season , consumer behaviour is shifting toward viewing indoor air quality as a year-round health priority rather than an emergency seasonal purchase.
According to industry leaders, adoption is gaining momentum well before peak pollution months.

Smart tech brand Qubo recorded a 150 percent growth over the previous year, while Xiaomi registered approximately 3X year-on-year sales growth during the festive period. Industry executives note that growing awareness surrounding indoor pollutants, ranging from dust and pet dander to everyday cooking and cleaning emissions, is encouraging households to take a proactive approach to home wellness throughout the year.

Retail footprint and online traffic reflect this expanding market footprint across the country. Electronics retailer Croma reported that air purifier sales volumes have more than doubled in 2026. While Delhi-NCR remains the dominant market, cities like Mumbai and regions beyond traditional high-pollution belts are showing sustained upticks.
Premium tech maker Dyson also reported that visits to its air purifier pages grew by over 100 percent in October compared to the same period last year.

Modern buyers are increasingly seeking advanced functionality and intelligent filtration tech. Croma highlighted strong consumer interest in models featuring real-time AQI displays, app controls, and multi-functional units combining purification with humidification or heating.

On e-commerce platforms, Amazon India reported that sales doubled over the past week. Shoppers are actively leveraging Rufus, Amazon’s personalised AI shopping assistant, to filter models by room size, filter type, and live sensor capabilities, prompting the e-retailer to expand selection on Amazon Now for immediate delivery.

articles.title: What to know about the online banking delays affecting major U.S. banks
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: A technical issue at JPMorgan Chase caused problems throughout the financial system on Monday (November 16, 2026), resulting in thousands of customers reporting difficulty accessing online accounts at several major U.S. banks and the money transfer service Zelle.

JPMorgan Chase, the largest U.S. bank by total assets, said a software bug was affecting its internal hardware systems and causing transaction delays. The company was working to bring banking services back online.
Some Chase customers received a message that said, "Some services aren't available. We're working on them. Please try back later."

In a sense, yes. Customers at Bank of America, Citigroup and other banks trying to transact with Chase may have seen their transactions slow, even though those banks were not having issues with their services.
"Other banks may have been impacted by slowness in transactions only to the extent that they were a party to a transaction with us," explained Joe Evangelisti, a spokesperson for Chase.
Zelle was not directly affected by the Chase glitch. But customers at other banks may have experienced transaction delays while trying to send or receive Zelle payments involving a Chase customer.

Zelle is a rapid peer-to-peer payment system used by major US banks. The platform is owned by Arizona-based Early Warning Services, which in turn is owned by financial institutions including Bank of America, Capital One, JPMorgan Chase, PNC Bank, Truist, US Bank and Wells Fargo.
A spokesperson for Early Warning Services said the Zelle network was fully operational.
Chase said that the technical problem was not the result of a cyberattack, stressing that it was an isolated incident and not related to anything other than a bug.
Chase said its customers still have access to their accounts and funds. The company expects the issue to be resolved by the end of day Monday.
No. While the disruptions took place just days apart, government officials and company leaders have said they were unrelated.

The major outage by Microsoft on Thursday (November 12, 2026) that lasted for hours, severely impacting services including Outlook, Teams and AI assistant Copilot, was due to a technical issue that arose during an upgrade. The tech giant has said there is "no indication" that the disruptions were caused by malicious activity, such as a cyberattack or due to action by artificial intelligence agents.

articles.title: Samsung led India’s smartphone market during Q3 2026, overall shipments collapsed 23%
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Apple stood at number four position with a 10.1% share, as the sharp decline across Chinese brands lifted its position in a shrinking market, even as Apple’s own shipments fell 25% YoY after a flat Q2

India’s smartphone market dropped by 23.3% year-over-year (YoY ) during Q3 2026 to reach 36.8 million units shipments. It was the steepest quarterly contraction since Q4 2022 and also the weakest festive quarter in a decade, said IDC.
The research firm credited rising memory chip costs, pushed up by AI-driven demands , tightened component availability for the decline that led a very little room for vendors to hold prices.

Smartphone’s average selling price (ASP) was at a record high ($371), a 26% YoY growth, festive offers were a few, and due to that price-sensitive buyers held back purchases this season, and pressure is likely to carry into Q4 2026.

Samsung emerged as the top smartphone brand with a 17.7% share during Q3, followed by Vivo with a 16.8% share and Oppo having a 13.3% share. Vivo had a nearly 30% drop in shipments compared to Q3 2025, while Oppo’s fell by around 27%.

Apple stood at number four position with a 10.1% share, as the sharp decline across Chinese brands lifted its position in a shrinking market, even as Apple’s own shipments fell 25% YoY after a flat Q2.

Supply shortages on the iPhone 15, 16 and 17, along with price increases around the September launches, weighed on volumes, and less offers on older-generation iPhones cooled demand from aspirational buyers.
iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max series contributed over 30% of Apple’s shipments, despite higher prices and no base iPhone 18.
Motorola came fifth with a 8.8% share while Xiaomi dropped to number six (8.3%), and Realme at seven (7.7%).

Chinese brands were hit hardest, as their reliance on entry-level and budget volumes limited their room to absorb higher costs. Most have, however, formed joint ventures with Indian manufacturers to scale up local production and benefit from government incentives, signalling their long-term commitment to India.
Shipments below $100 plunged 90.9% YoY to just 0.7 million units, and the tier’s share fell from 16.2% to 1.9%, a segment that has effectively left the market.

4G shipments declined 15.5% YoY against 24.1% for 5G, nudging 4G’s share up to 10.4% from 9.5%. The gain comes from 5G falling faster as vendors retained 4G options at entry-level price points, with no sign of renewed 4G demand.

The $200–400 band held flat (+0.1% YoY) in a shrinking market, while $400–600 surged 79.8%. Together they now account for 42.9% of shipments, up from 29.9%, helped by financing options that narrowed the price gap between bands. The $100–200 mass-budget segment fell 21.3% YoY, yet its 40.6% share keeps it the single largest band.

articles.title: Bird flu confirmed at two farms in Keralam’s Alappuzha; 26,000 birds to be culled
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Six rapid response teams of Animal Husbandry and Health departments set to carry out culling

Bird flu has been confirmed at two poultry farms in Alappuzha district of Keralam, and authorities will begin culling around 26,000 birds on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) to prevent the spread of the infection, officials said.

Around 26,000 domestic birds within a 1-km radius of the affected farms in Ambalappuzha North, Ambalappuzha South and Chennithala panchayats are likely to be culled, they said on Tuesday (November 17, 2026).
The infection was detected among quails and chickens at a farm in Ward 11 of Ambalappuzha North and among ducks and chickens at a farm in Ward 1 of Chennithala panchayat.
Samples collected from the farms tested positive for bird flu at the National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (NIHSAD) in Bhopal.
According to a preliminary estimate, 10,044 birds in Ambalappuzha North alone will have to be culled as part of the operation.
Six rapid response teams of the Animal Husbandry and Health departments will carry out the culling on Wednesday.
Each team will comprise a doctor, two livestock inspectors, two attendants and four workers.
Representatives of the local panchayats, police, revenue officials and local body employees will also assist the teams.
Two additional teams have been kept on standby, officials said.
An area within a 10-km radius of the affected farms has been declared a surveillance zone.
District Collector Shaji V Nair convened an emergency meeting to review the situation and coordinate preventive measures.

Deputy Collector (Disaster Management) S Biju, Chief Veterinary Officer Dr P Rajeev and officials from the Health, Police, Local Self-Government, Food Safety and Motor Vehicles departments attended the meeting.

articles.title: Archana Veeramani complains to Madras High Court about SIT digging up her bungalow swimming pool without notice
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Justice V. Lakshminarayanan directs SIT to allow her lawyer to be present, away from earshot distance, during her interrogation

Serial child sexual abuse case accused ‘Gem Granites’ R. Veeramani’ s daughter Archana Veeramani on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) complained to the Madras High Court that a Special Investigation Team (SIT) had dug up the swimming pool in her house on Saturday (November 14) in search of a body of a child victim but could not find anything.

Appearing before Justice V. Lakshminarayanan, senior counsel Nitya Ramakrishnan, representing Ms. Archana, said, the police had carried out the excavation operation in the residential house at Chennai without any notice either to her client or her aged mother who has been residing over there ever since the accused got arrested on August 29 .

The counsel insisted that the SIT must be directed to issue an advance notice to Ms. Archana before carrying out any such operation in the residential premises and also allow her lawyer to be present. She questioned as to how the police could indulge in such a rampage in a residential property occupied by two women with one of them being an elderly person.

However, Additional Public Prosecutor Arun Anbumani told the court the police had not entered the building in which the two women were residing and the excavation was carried out only in the open area. He said, the operation was necessitated since a car driver had given a statement that the body of one of the child victims was buried in the bungalow.

After hearing both sides, the judge said, the court could not direct the SIT to issue advance notice while carrying out certain activities as part of the investigation. He, however, ordered that if the police wished to interrogate the two women at their residence, they should permit Ms. Archana’s lawyer to be present away from earshot distance.

The judge also extended till November 24 the time granted to the SIT to file its counter affidavit to a writ petition filed by Ms. Archana accusing the SIT of having indulged in human rights violations when she was forced to deboard from an airplane , bound to Singapore for her son’s medical treatment, on October 23, without any valid authorisation.

Ms. Archana claimed she was not an accused in that case and no court had restrained her from undertaking foreign travel. Yet, the airplane staff had forcefully deboarded her from the airplane, at the instance of the SIT officials, without assigning any reason and she was taken to the office of the SIT for inquiry without considering her health condition, she said.

Stating she was suffering from multiple sclerosis, a chronic autoimmune condition that affects the central nervous system, for about 20 years, the petitioner said she collapsed on the floor of the SIT office and lost control over her bladder. All these events were video recorded by the police despite objections and she was shifted to a hospital for treatment only on the advice of her doctor friend, the petitioner added.

articles.title: Three men arrested for illegal sand mining from Palar riverbed in Vellore
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: According to the police, the gang reportedly confessed that the sand was mined from dry riverbed to sell the consignment to retail traders.
Three persons were arrested by Tiruvalam police near Katpadi in Vellore for illegally mining sand from the dry riverbed of Palar on Monday (November 16, 2026).
Police identified the arrested persons as K. Sekar (45), R. Viswanathan (32) and G. Munusamy (37). They are residents of Sekkadu village near Katpadi.

Initial inquiry revealed that special teams were formed in the district to prevent illegal sand mining, smuggling of ganja and other banned substances and petty crime. A police team that was on routine patrol along the river near Katpadi spotted tractors and earthmover in the dry riverbed. The police also found two tractors with loads of river sand.

According to the police, the gang reportedly confessed that the sand was mined from dry riverbed to sell the consignment to retail traders. They were arrested. Two tractors and an earthmover were seized from them.

articles.title: ASEAN Summit LIVE updates: President Trump arrives in Manila to hold discussions with Quad leaders
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: In the first Quad Summit since 2024, PM Modi is expected to meet U.S. President Trump, Japanese PM Takaichi and Australian PM Albanese
U.S. President Donald Trump arrived in Manila today, where he is scheduled to meet regional partners, talk trade, and seek a break from a series of setbacks at home.

Upon his arrival, Mr. Trump was welcomed by Philippine Executive Secretary Ralph Recto, Ilocos Norte Representative and presidential son Sandro Marcos, Philippine Ambassador to the United States Jose Manuel Romualdez, U.S. Ambassador to the Philippines Lee Lipton and Pasay City Mayor Emi Calixto.

Manila is Mr. Trump’s first stop on a three-day trip that will later take him to China for historic three-way nuclear talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin, and, according to Mr. Trump, potentially for a meeting with North Korea’s leader Kim Jong Un.
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has proposed the creation of an Asian energy agency to help countries in the region cope with oil crises.
Ms. Takaichi called for setting up an oil security task force and a Japan-based version of the International Energy Agency for the region.
“We would like to position this as an Asian version of the IEA,” she said.
U.S. President Donald Trump will sign a joint statement with Thailand’s premier today, marking “significant progress” in trade negotiations, but will not ink a final deal, a Thai official said.
A framework agreement was unveiled just over a year ago, on the same day as Trump announced a short-lived ceasefire between Thailand and its neighbour Cambodia following deadly border clashes.

Amid ASEAN members grappling with fuel shortages and price hikes, Japanese PM Sanae Takaichi said her country’s “hydro-tanks” would be available for use to the ASEAN countries under the proposed initiative for cooperation on oil stockpiling.

articles.title: SIR row: Supreme Court agrees to hear INDIA bloc’s ‘interrogatories’ on ‘nationwide SIR’, CEC
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The affidavit asserted that the massive exercise (SIR), in which approximately 13 crore voters were excluded, was a unanimous decision of the ECI

The Supreme Court on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) agreed to have a detailed hearing of an application filed by Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and INDIA bloc leaders, who have posed 48 ‘interrogatories’ to Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, and senior poll officials regarding the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

The interrogatories challenge the veracity of “bare assertions” made by the Election Commission of India (ECI) in an October 26 affidavit that the decision to hold a nationwide SIR, which saw around 13 crore voters excluded from the electoral rolls, was “unanimous”.

A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant posted the case for December 9 after senior advocate Harish Salve, appearing for the ECI, enquired if the court would have enough time to hear the multiple petitions in the post-lunch session.

Senior advocates Kapil Sibal, A.M. Singhvi and advocate Prasanna S., for the INDIA bloc leaders, urged the Bench, which was about to rise for lunch after the morning session when Mr. Salve intervened, to issue notice on the application containing the interrogatories.

Though, initially, the court agreed to issue notice to the ECI for a response, Mr. Salve, along with senior advocate Maninder Singh, opposed the issuance of any notice before a preliminary hearing on the application.
“We will then hear the application and pass necessary orders,” the CJI said.

The application was filed as part of the Opposition leaders’ writ petition claiming the nationwide SIR exercise, the manner and extent of its conduct, was the product of a unilateral exercise of power by the CEC without the knowledge, approval or concurrence of the Election Commissioners.

Mr. Gandhi and the Opposition leaders submitted that posing the interrogatories was necessary as the controversy in their petition substantially rested upon facts that lie exclusively within the knowledge and the records of the ECI. The petitioners said they had no means of access to those facts except through the ECI and their officials.
So far, rather than disclosing those facts, the ECI has only made bare assertions.

The Opposition leaders said though the Supreme Court was not fettered by any rigid procedure, ‘interrogatories’ were recognised by the Supreme Court Rules Further, the court was empowered by the Rules to pass any orders “necessary for the ends of justice or to prevent abuse of the process of the court”.

The interrogatories covered detailed ground, including whether the October 26 affidavit claiming that SIR was a “unanimous decision”, was ever placed before Mr. Sandhu and Mr. Joshi. If so, when and how, and if they had suggested any changes in any assertions made in the document.

The Opposition leaders have asked for the number of the file clearing a nationwide SIR in which the decision of the Commission was taken, the date of the decision, whether it was taken at a meeting, upon circulation of a file or through electronic means, and the date on which each member signified approval.

SIR row: Supreme Court agrees to hear INDIA bloc’s ‘interrogatories’ on ‘nationwide SIR’, CEC

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

The affidavit asserted that the massive exercise (SIR), in which approximately 13 crore voters were excluded, was a unanimous decision of the ECI

The Supreme Court on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) agreed to have a detailed hearing of an application filed by Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and INDIA bloc leaders, who have posed 48 ‘interrogatories’ to Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, and senior poll officials regarding the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

The interrogatories challenge the veracity of “bare assertions” made by the Election Commission of India (ECI) in an October 26 affidavit that the decision to hold a nationwide SIR, which saw around 13 crore voters excluded from the electoral rolls, was “unanimous”.

A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant posted the case for December 9 after senior advocate Harish Salve, appearing for the ECI, enquired if the court would have enough time to hear the multiple petitions in the post-lunch session.

Senior advocates Kapil Sibal, A.M. Singhvi and advocate Prasanna S., for the INDIA bloc leaders, urged the Bench, which was about to rise for lunch after the morning session when Mr. Salve intervened, to issue notice on the application containing the interrogatories.

Though, initially, the court agreed to issue notice to the ECI for a response, Mr. Salve, along with senior advocate Maninder Singh, opposed the issuance of any notice before a preliminary hearing on the application.

“We will then hear the application and pass necessary orders,” the CJI said.

The application was filed as part of the Opposition leaders’ writ petition claiming the nationwide SIR exercise, the manner and extent of its conduct, was the product of a unilateral exercise of power by the CEC without the knowledge, approval or concurrence of the Election Commissioners.

Mr. Gandhi and the Opposition leaders submitted that posing the interrogatories was necessary as the controversy in their petition substantially rested upon facts that lie exclusively within the knowledge and the records of the ECI. The petitioners said they had no means of access to those facts except through the ECI and their officials.

So far, rather than disclosing those facts, the ECI has only made bare assertions.

The Opposition leaders said though the Supreme Court was not fettered by any rigid procedure, ‘interrogatories’ were recognised by the Supreme Court Rules Further, the court was empowered by the Rules to pass any orders “necessary for the ends of justice or to prevent abuse of the process of the court”.

The interrogatories covered detailed ground, including whether the October 26 affidavit claiming that SIR was a “unanimous decision”, was ever placed before Mr. Sandhu and Mr. Joshi. If so, when and how, and if they had suggested any changes in any assertions made in the document.

The Opposition leaders have asked for the number of the file clearing a nationwide SIR in which the decision of the Commission was taken, the date of the decision, whether it was taken at a meeting, upon circulation of a file or through electronic means, and the date on which each member signified approval.

articles.title: IOC gets government nod for commercial sustainable aviation fuel supply from Panipat refinery
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The State-run refiner plans to enter into supply agreements with airlines before committing investments to additional SAF projects

State-owned Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) has secured government approvals to commercially supply sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) from its Panipat refinery in north India, with the facility capable of producing enough fuel to meet the country's 1 per cent blending target for international flights in 2027, Chairman A.S. Sahney said on Tuesday (November 17, 2026).

The State-run refiner plans to enter into supply agreements with airlines before committing investments to additional SAF projects, Mr. Sahney said at an industry event, signalling a demand-led approach to expanding production capacity as India prepares to introduce low-carbon fuel requirements for international aviation.

IOC's Panipat facility is positioned to meet the initial blending mandate, Mr. Sahney said, although he did not specify the volume of fuel covered by the government approvals or when commercial supplies would begin.

In August, an IOC executive had said the company expected to begin operations at its first SAF plant at Panipat within two months and was looking to take an investment decision on a second facility within five to six months.

The refinery, which has a crude processing capacity of about 301,000 barrels per day, received India's first International Sustainability and Carbon Certification (ISCC) CORSIA certification for SAF production in 2025, enabling it to produce fuel meeting internationally-recognised sustainability requirements for aviation.

IOC has planned to produce about 35,000 tonnes of SAF annually from used cooking oil at the facility, sourcing feedstock from large hotel and restaurant chains. The company has also signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Air India for SAF supplies, although the agreement did not specify a commencement date or volumes.
The Panipat project forms part of India's broader effort to introduce sustainable fuels into aviation, a sector seeking to reduce its carbon footprint while accommodating growing air travel demand.

India is targeting a 1 per cent SAF blending requirement in fuel supplied for international flights from 2027, rising to 2 per cent in 2028. The targets are aligned with the global push to reduce aviation emissions under the International Civil Aviation Organization's Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA).

SAF can be produced from non-petroleum feedstocks such as used cooking oil and agricultural waste and can be blended with conventional jet fuel. It offers airlines a way to lower lifecycle carbon emissions without requiring wholesale changes to existing aircraft or airport fuelling infrastructure.

IOC is also developing a separate SAF production facility using alcohol-to-jet (ATJ) technology, with planned annual capacity of 86,800 tonnes. The project, being developed with US-based LanzaJet, will use ethanol as feedstock and is targeted for completion by March 2028.

The expansion would diversify IOC's SAF production beyond used cooking oil and add capacity as blending requirements increase. However, the availability and cost of sustainable feedstocks, alongside long-term purchase commitments from airlines, will be important factors in determining the pace of investment and commercial adoption.
IOC's Panipat refinery is also undergoing an expansion to increase its conventional oil-product processing capacity by 200,000 barrels per day by 2027.

articles.title: Japan offers ASEAN nations access to energy storage
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: ASEAN members have been grappling with fuel shortages and price hikes after the West Asia conflict squeezed the flow of crude to the region
Japan said on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) that Southeast Asian nations will be able to access its crude oil storage facilities as part of efforts to prepare the region for a future energy crisis.
The announcement came as leaders of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) met in Manila, where energy security has been high on the agenda.
Keep track | ASEAN Summit LIVE updates: PM Modi at ASEAN-India Summit; Quad meeting likely after President Trump arrives
Addressing regional leaders, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said her country's "hydro-tanks" would be available for use under the proposed initiative for cooperation on oil stockpiling.
ASEAN members have been grappling with fuel shortages and price hikes after the West Asia conflict squeezed the flow of crude to the region.
The regional bloc has previously called for "unimpeded" passage through the Strait of Hormuz, which was closed following U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran.
Under the Japanese POWERR Asia initiative, ASEAN nations will be able to use Japan's excess storage capacity for crude oil.

"We have suggested to utilise our crude oil stockpiling facilities in Japan, which is not utilised," Japan's Foreign Ministry press secretary Toshihiro Kitamura told reporters on the sidelines of the ASEAN summit.
"By utilising those unused facilities in Japan, we can stockpile the other countries' crude oil and in case of crisis... it's a kind of joint stockpiling system."
Japan has 254 days' worth of oil reserves, Mr. Kitamura said, while at the outbreak of the West Asia war in February some ASEAN countries had less than a month's worth.
An ASEAN-backed study for joint stockpiling of oil has also recommended using facilities in Thailand and Indonesia, but Kitamura said a final decision had not been made.
"But as a government in Japan, we are ready to work with ASEAN countries to utilise our own facilities," he said.

articles.title: Pakistan, Iran stress sustained engagement, coordination for regional stability
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Field Marshal Munir made the remarks during a meeting with a high-level Iranian delegation led by Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi in Rawalpindi

Pakistan's Chief of Defence Forces Asim Munir has stressed the importance of sustained engagement and close coordination with Iran to promote regional peace and stability, the army said on Tuesday (November 17, 2026).

Field Marshal Munir, who is also the Chief of Army Staff, made the remarks during a meeting with a high-level Iranian delegation led by Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi in Rawalpindi on Monday (November 16), according to a statement by the Pakistan Army.

The two sides "underscored the importance of sustained engagement, mutual trust and close coordination between the two brotherly countries for promoting regional peace and stability," the statement said.
Mr. Araghchi appreciated Pakistan's constructive role in promoting regional peace and stability and expressed Iran's desire to further strengthen bilateral relations, it said.
The two sides also exchanged views on exploring avenues to address common security challenges.

The remarks come amid continuing tensions in West Asia following the outbreak of a military conflict on February 28, when joint U.S.-Israeli strikes killed Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and several senior political and military officials.

Iran subsequently launched large-scale retaliatory missile and drone attacks on Gulf countries hosting U.S. military facilities, including the UAE, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain and Saudi Arabia. The attacks disrupted regional airspace and damaged civilian and energy infrastructure.

The conflict has also severely disrupted commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, a key global energy route through which a significant share of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas supplies passes.
Pakistan played a key mediating role in efforts to end the hostilities, with an interim agreement, known as the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding, signed between Washington and Tehran in June.
The interim agreement envisaged an end to military operations, the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and the lifting of the U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports.

However, the arrangement failed to produce a lasting settlement, with the two sides unable to bridge differences over sanctions relief, the naval blockade, shipping arrangements through the Strait of Hormuz and Iran's nuclear programme.
The 60-day period envisaged for negotiations towards a final settlement expired without an agreement.

articles.title: Leaders, protesters await Donald Trump arrival for Manila summit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Around 2,000 demonstrators were already facing off with riot shield-wielding police while carrying banners reading Trump out now and Reject Pax Silica

Thousands were set to protest in Manila against Donald Trump on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) ahead of his arrival at a summit that the U.S. leader will seek to dominate despite bruising election losses.

Around 2,000 demonstrators were already facing off with riot shield-wielding police while carrying banners reading "Trump out now" and "Reject Pax Silica", a reference to a U.S. supply chain initiative that has divided opinions in the Philippines.

The U.S. president's streamlined agenda will send him straight to a meeting of the so-called Quad security alliance, with India's Narendra Modi, Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi of Japan and Australia's Anthony Albanese.

The gathering on the sidelines of the 11-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations leaders' summit marks the first by the group's leaders since Trump's January 2025 return to power, and comes days after his Republican party took a drubbing in midterm elections.

While the Quad -- broadly aimed at counterbalancing China's regional influence -- has quietly progressed in deepening coordination, the short time allotted for Tuesday's (November 17, 2026) meeting meant it was unlikely to extend beyond pleasantries, Ryan Hass of the Brookings Institution told AFP .
The timing, however, carried significance, he said, given the historical meeting Trump will attend with the leaders of China and Russia in just two days.
"It's a way of inoculating Trump against criticism of caving to authoritarians when he meets with Xi (Jinping) and (Vladimir) Putin in Shenzhen," Mr. Hass said.
Hayley Channer, economic security director at the Sydney-based United States Studies Centre, said Mr. Trump's decision to include ASEAN on his travel agenda was noteworthy.
"Southeast Asia has never been a high priority for the United States, so President Trump travelling to Manila is significant," she added.
A spokesman for Japan's foreign ministry said the Quad agenda would include discussions of the East and South China Sea -- areas where multiple parties have overlapping claims with China.
Mr. Trump will later attend a meeting with ASEAN heads of state before going to a gala dinner.
While ASEAN leaders have spent three days grappling with a raft of regional issues, the spectre of Mr. Trump's ongoing tariff blitz has loomed large.

articles.title: Nvidia to reveal first earnings since spy scandal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Investors will closely scrutinize the results for indications the artificial intelligence boom can withstand the crisis
AI chip giant Nvidia reports its first earnings on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) since a spy scandal forced co-founder Jensen Huang to quit and the United States to tighten export curbs on chips.
Investors will closely scrutinize the results for indications the artificial intelligence boom can withstand the crisis, which highlighted a loophole allegedly exploited by Chinese companies.

Mr. Huang, perhaps the tech industry's most recognised booster of AI, stepped down on November 12 following revelations of extramarital affairs, including with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.

The scandal has battered shares of Nvidia -- until recently the world's most valuable publicly traded company -- which is at the centre of an AI buildout that has helped propel markets to record highs and boosted economic growth around the globe.

Washington announced new restrictions on Monday (November 16) on AI chip exports, drawing condemnation from Beijing just before the high-profile APEC summit where U.S. President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping are set for talks.
Beijing's Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said: "China will take necessary measures to resolutely safeguard its legitimate rights and interests".

The new U.S. export curbs and the wider Nvidia scandal risk casting a shadow over Mr. Trump and Mr. Xi's talks at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting, which starts Wednesday in the Chinese city of Shenzhen.

Under Washington's new rules, data centres anywhere in the world will need a U.S. license to provide large volumes of computing power from advanced chips to companies headquartered in China, Macau or other countries under U.S. arms embargoes.

The rules also require licenses to ship advanced chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil -- countries the U.S. commerce department says present a "higher-than-normal risk of diversion" of the chips.

The changes are a response to a loophole that allowed Chinese firms to rent AI computing power from data centers in Southeast Asia and elsewhere that run on U.S. hardware not available for export to China.
While the loophole has been known to authorities, the revelation of Mr. Huang's affair has drawn intense scrutiny to the practice.

His lover Alice Huang, who is not related to the 63-year-old, is a former executive of Megaspeed -- a Singapore-based cloud computing firm under US criminal investigation for allegedly helping Chinese companies procure advanced Nvidia AI chips in circumvention of export controls.

articles.title: In line with WHO framework, T.N.’s National Centre of Ageing provides integrated care for the elderly
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: WHO’s approach is to provide a continuum of integrated care that helps to reorient health and social services towards more person-centred and coordinated care

Maintaining physical and mental capacities is key to ensuring that older persons remain functionally independent. With age-related conditions such as visual and hearing impairment, memory and mobility issues often remaining undetected or unaddressed in the elderly, the National Centre of Ageing (NCA), Guindy has started to focus on providing integrated care to help older persons maintain functional ability. This is in line with the World Health Organisation’s (WHO) integrated care for older people approach (ICOPE).

According to the WHO, numerous physiological changes occur, and the risks of experiencing a decline in physical and mental capacities (intrinsic capacity) and having more than one condition (disease) increase when people age. This could manifest as cognitive decline, limited mobility, hearing loss, malnutrition, vision impairment, depressive symptoms, urinary incontinence and falls. ICOPE is WHO’s approach to provide a continuum of integrated care that helps to reorient health and social services towards more person-centred and coordinated care. It supports optimising intrinsic capacity and functional ability in older age, it said.

articles.title: ASEAN Summit LIVE updates: Quad announces Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Quad is a ‘trusted partnership’ delivering solutions, says PM Modi

The Quad grouping, following its meeting in Manila, announced the ‘Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration’ which is “ a new initiative to enhance information sharing and maritime domain awareness”
“In 2027, our respective P-8 and P-3C patrol aircraft are scheduled to fly in a maritime exercise for the first time in a Quad context, making our seas safer,” the statement added.
In a joint press release following the Quad meeting in Manila, the group said that it “affirms the importance of the AI Accelerator, announced by our Foreign Ministers in Atlanta.”
“The Accelerator is intended to coordinate and fund efforts to support trusted AI access, deployment, and technical assistance across the Indo-Pacific,” it added.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi discussed ways to strengthen cooperation and exchanged views on regional and global developments with his counterparts from Singapore and Thailand in separate bilateral meetings in the Philippines.

Mr. Modi, who arrived in Manila on Monday to attend the ASEAN-India Summit and East Asia Summit, met Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong and Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul on the sidelines of the two summits.
PM Modi, at the Quad meeting in Manila, announced that the inaugural Quad Business Leaders Forum will be hosted in Mumbai in 2027, the Ministry of External Affairs said.

The Ministry of External Affairs said that at the Quad meeting, PM Modi “reaffirmed India’s commitment to a constructive and reliable Quad partnership, advancing peace, prosperity and resilience in the Indo-Pacific through cooperation in maritime security, economic security, critical technologies and disaster response.”

U.S. President Donald Trump confirmed four key outcomes of the Quad leaders’ meeting in Manila, covering economic cooperation, artificial intelligence, maritime security and cybersecurity, as leaders of India, the United States, Japan and Australia gathered for the high-level engagement.
The four outcomes include the Quad Business Leaders’ Forum, Super Intelligence Accelerator, Maritime Intelligence Sharing Corporation and Quad cybersecurity intelligence-sharing cooperation.

Addressing the leaders, Trump highlighted the growing importance of the four-nation grouping and announced initiatives to strengthen commercial ties, advance superintelligence and enhance maritime cooperation.

Highlighting their strategic importance, he described the four countries as “the four corners of a free, open, stable, and prosperous Indo-Pacific”, adding that they coordinated closely on regional security, economic security and diplomacy.

articles.title: NPP seeks Governor's intervention on Wildlife Protection Act's applicability in Nagaland
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The National People's Party said its concern was to ensure that wildlife protection measures were implemented in conformity with the constitutional safeguards available to Nagaland

The National People's Party (NPP) has urged the Nagaland Governor to initiate a comprehensive constitutional and legal examination of the applicability of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, and its subsequent amendments in the State in the context of Article 371A of the Constitution.

In a representation submitted to the Governor on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), NPP national vice-president Vevoyi Wideo sought verification of the Nagaland Legislative Assembly's resolution of September 18, 1981, through which the Act was adopted, along with the relevant Gazette notification and subsequent official records.

The party said the Act had undergone major amendments in 1991, 2002, 2006 and 2022, raising questions about the legal basis for applying the amended provisions in Nagaland, particularly where they may affect matters protected under Article 371A.

The constitutional provision safeguards Naga religious and social practices, customary laws and procedures, and ownership and transfer of land and its resources from the application of Parliamentary legislation unless the Nagaland Legislative Assembly so decides by a resolution.

The NPP observed that hunting and the relationship of Naga communities with their natural environment are, in various local contexts, linked to customary practices, community traditions and village-level regulatory systems.

Clarifying that it did not question the importance of wildlife conservation, the party said its concern was to ensure that wildlife protection measures were implemented in conformity with the constitutional safeguards available to Nagaland.

It also pointed to the absence of authoritative clarification on the issue, which it said had created uncertainty among enforcement agencies and local communities, potentially leading to avoidable disputes and tensions.

The NPP urged the Governor to refer the matter to the State government for examination in consultation with the departments concerned and bring it to the attention of the competent authorities, including the Speaker of the Nagaland Legislative Assembly.

The party further sought a reasoned examination of the applicability of the four amendment Acts and whether any fresh Assembly resolution, legislative clarification or other lawful measure was required.

It also proposed consideration of a Nagaland-specific administrative or legislative framework to address the relationship between wildlife conservation and recognised Naga customary practices. The representation requested that the party be informed of the action taken on the issues raised.

NPP seeks Governor's intervention on Wildlife Protection Act's applicability in Nagaland

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

The National People's Party said its concern was to ensure that wildlife protection measures were implemented in conformity with the constitutional safeguards available to Nagaland

The National People's Party (NPP) has urged the Nagaland Governor to initiate a comprehensive constitutional and legal examination of the applicability of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, and its subsequent amendments in the State in the context of Article 371A of the Constitution.

In a representation submitted to the Governor on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), NPP national vice-president Vevoyi Wideo sought verification of the Nagaland Legislative Assembly's resolution of September 18, 1981, through which the Act was adopted, along with the relevant Gazette notification and subsequent official records.

The party said the Act had undergone major amendments in 1991, 2002, 2006 and 2022, raising questions about the legal basis for applying the amended provisions in Nagaland, particularly where they may affect matters protected under Article 371A.

The constitutional provision safeguards Naga religious and social practices, customary laws and procedures, and ownership and transfer of land and its resources from the application of Parliamentary legislation unless the Nagaland Legislative Assembly so decides by a resolution.

The NPP observed that hunting and the relationship of Naga communities with their natural environment are, in various local contexts, linked to customary practices, community traditions and village-level regulatory systems.

Clarifying that it did not question the importance of wildlife conservation, the party said its concern was to ensure that wildlife protection measures were implemented in conformity with the constitutional safeguards available to Nagaland.

It also pointed to the absence of authoritative clarification on the issue, which it said had created uncertainty among enforcement agencies and local communities, potentially leading to avoidable disputes and tensions.

The NPP urged the Governor to refer the matter to the State government for examination in consultation with the departments concerned and bring it to the attention of the competent authorities, including the Speaker of the Nagaland Legislative Assembly.

The party further sought a reasoned examination of the applicability of the four amendment Acts and whether any fresh Assembly resolution, legislative clarification or other lawful measure was required.

It also proposed consideration of a Nagaland-specific administrative or legislative framework to address the relationship between wildlife conservation and recognised Naga customary practices. The representation requested that the party be informed of the action taken on the issues raised.

articles.title: Specialised maternal and child healthcare institute launched in Hyderabad
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Apollo Hospitals on Tuesday inaugurated the Apollo Institute of Parents and Children at its Financial District facility in Hyderabad, expanding its specialised healthcare services for women, mothers, newborns and children. The institute was inaugurated by Apollo Hospitals Projects director, Upasana Kamineni Konidela.

The facility has a dedicated obstetrics wing, a Level III Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) and an attached perinatal centre to provide comprehensive care for mothers and newborns, including those with high-risk pregnancies and premature babies. The institute offers integrated services covering fertility counselling, fetal assessments, high-risk pregnancy management, maternity care, specialised labour and delivery services, and general paediatric care.

Pointing to the need to address women’s health beyond childbirth, Ms. Upasana said society often celebrated pregnancy and delivery but overlooked the physical and emotional challenges women faced during the fourth trimester. Comprehensive care and support should be available from the first trimester through the fourth trimester, she added.

Senior consultant gynaecologist Phani Jyothsana said the institute aims to provide personalised, multidisciplinary healthcare for women at every stage of life, alongside specialised services for newborns and children. Another senior consultant gynaecologist, Pujitha Devi, said the NICU also incorporates Kangaroo Mother Care to support the health and development of newborns.

articles.title: Cyclone 'Akvan' LIVE updates: Akvan likely to become a severe cyclonic storm by November 19
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The clouds associated with the system are projected to bring light to moderate rainfall at some parts of Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and West Bengal

The cyclonic storm “Akvan”, formed over the central parts of the southern Bay of Bengal and the adjoining west-central Bay of Bengal, is very likely to intensify into a Severe Cyclonic Storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal by this evening. Thereafter, it is likely to intensify further into a Very Severe Cyclonic Storm by the morning of 19 November.

Cyclone Akvan brings heavy to extremely heavy rainfall over Tamil Nadu (17–18 November), Coastal Andhra Pradesh (19–20 November), and Odisha (21 November), alongside gusty winds in the Bay of Bengal, according to IMD.
The State government has stepped up its preparedness to deal with Cyclone Akvan over the Bay of Bengal.
Andhra Pradesh Home Minister Vangalapudi Anitha directed officials to take precautionary measures in all coastal districts to prevent loss of life and property.
Andhra Home Minister Vangalapudi Anitha put coastal districts on high alert ahead of Cyclone Akvan’s landfall between Nellore and Tuni, and warned fishermen.
Cyclone Akvan is likely to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm over Bay of Bengal by the morning of 19 November 2026.
Very slow north-northwestward movement of Cyclone Akvan over central parts of South and adjoining Westcentral BoB at 0830 IST of today.
It will become a Severe Cyclone tonight, moving northwestwards become Very Severe Cyclone on 19 evening, to cross Andhra Pradesh coast around 20th noon.

Cyclone Akvan, expected to form over the Bay of Bengal on Monday evening, is very likely to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Nellore and Tuni by noon on November 20 as a very severe cyclonic storm, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said in its forecast on Monday (November 16, 2026). Winds at landfall may reach 120-130 kmph, gusting to 145 kmph.
Cyclone Akvan is likely to hit the Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Tuni by noon on November 20 with winds of up to 145 kmph. Check its path here.

The Odisha government yesterday geared up for the possible impact of Cyclone Akvan, the third cyclonic storm formed over the Bay of Bengal in three weeks, with the deployment of 74 rescue teams and early evacuation of vulnerable people in the southern districts.
Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari held a meeting to review preparedness based on the latest IMD forecast and said the government made “full arrangements to secure lives and property”.

articles.title: T.N. Ministers meet Union Ministers; seek Centre’s support for infrastructure projects, pending dues
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Aadhav Arjuna seeks financial assistance for maritime projects; Rajmohan highlights pending dues

Minister for Public Works and Sports Development Aadhav Arjuna on Tuesday met Union Minister for Ports, Shipping and Waterways Sarbananda Sonowal in New Delhi and submitted a memorandum seeking financial assistance for key maritime infrastructure development projects in Tamil Nadu.

During the meeting, Mr. Arjuna sought ₹118 crore for the development of Rameswaram Port and the launch of international passenger ferry services between Rameswaram and Talaimannar in Sri Lanka; ₹4,700 crore for the development of Cuddalore Greenfield Deep Sea Port; and ₹900 crore for the construction of promenades and boat jetties at Marina in Chennai and Mamallapuram, and the launch of passenger ferry services between Chennai and Puducherry.

He also sought ₹2,700 crore for the rehabilitation and deepening of National Waterway IV (Buckingham Canal) and ₹1,200 crore for deepening the Pamban channel to 10 metres to connect the western and eastern coastal regions.

Meanwhile, Minister for School Education Rajmohan met Union Minister for Education Pralhad Joshi in New Delhi and submitted a memorandum regarding pending dues to Tamil Nadu and other schemes. Mr. Joshi posted on X that the deliberations included key priorities of the State, including matters relating to Samagra Shiksha and Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas. He said the meeting reaffirmed the commitment to strengthening school education and ensuring inclusive growth for students across Tamil Nadu.

articles.title: Prakasam tobacco farmers fear Cyclone Akvan after suffering losses from Arnab, Murasu
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Farmers who lost curing barns worth lakhs of rupees to Cyclone Murasu say they have received no relief from the government or insurance companies

Several tobacco farmers in the coastal villages of combined Prakasam district have suffered losses due to the back-to-back cyclones Arnab and Murasu. However, they have received no relief from either the government or insurance companies and are now worried about Cyclone Akvan.

Strong winds and heavy rain severely damaged tobacco barns (also called curing barns or tobacco sheds, used for drying and curing harvested tobacco leaves). They also wetted tobacco bales, which will be penalised or rejected at auction centres.

Molakalapalli Sambasiva Rao, a tobacco farmer from Ammanabrolu village in Naguluppalapadu mandal of Prakasam district, said, “We cultivate tobacco in 7-8 acres on lease basis. Tobacco barn worth ₹10 lakh was damaged because of the gale triggered by Cyclone Murasu.”

He said the rain caused excess moisture, which ruins the quality of the tobacco leaf. The wet tobacco bales will be destroyed. Since the tobacco farmers are preparing for the next harvesting season, they are afraid of the likely impact of Cyclone Akvan.

Meanwhile, in view of the heavy rain alert, Prakasam District Collector P. Raja Babu directed the Agriculture Department officials and farmers to take proactive measures to mitigate potential damage and minimise the losses.

“Tobacco must be purchased at the prices stipulated by the government. The farmers who have cultivated tobacco without obtaining the necessary permissions will not be paid the government-mandated prices and action will be taken against them,” the Collector said.

As the district is likely to receive heavy rainfall, the Collector has directed the officials concerned to hold detailed discussions with private companies and take appropriate measures regarding the procurement of tobacco.

The Agriculture Department has stationed special officers at tobacco auction centres. The farmers were asked to consult them during the procurement process and follow their advice. A survey will soon be conducted in each mandal to identify the tobacco farmers and their crop.

Speaking to The Hindu , Tobacco Board Regional Manager G.L.K. Prasad said, “Tobacco production and e-auctions are regulated by the Tobacco Board under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. The licensed tobacco growers must go for the crop insurance.”

“The Tobacco Board has authorised production of 85 million kg in the Southern Black Soils (SBS) and Southern Light Soils (SLS) region, but the farmers have produced nearly double at 150 million kg. The farmers who are illegally cultivating 65 million kg cannot claim insurance,” he said.

articles.title: Violent protests erupt in Hasina’s hometown as tensions rise over her proposed return to Bangladesh
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The protests come amid renewed tensions over Ms. Hasina’s proposed return from India, where she has been staying since fleeing Bangladesh in August 2024 after a student-led uprising toppled her government

Supporters of deposed Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina ’s Awami League party staged violent demonstrations in her hometown of Gopalganj on Sunday (November 15, 2026), attacking police vehicles and installations amid growing political tensions over her stated plan to return to the country in December.
Editorial | In a dilemma: On Sheikh Hasina and India-Bangladesh ties

The protests come amid renewed tensions over Ms. Hasina’s proposed return from India, where she has been staying since fleeing Bangladesh in August 2024 after a student-led uprising toppled her government.

Ms. Hasina was sentenced to death in absentia by Bangladesh’s International Crimes Tribunal in November 2025 for crimes against humanity over her government’s crackdown on protesters. She has rejected the charges and the proceedings.
Ms. Hasina, 79, has repeatedly said since July that she intends to return to Bangladesh in December and face legal proceedings, despite the death sentence against her.

The Bangladesh government has been seeking her extradition from India under a bilateral treaty. It has also declined a request made by a London-based law firm on Ms. Hasina’s behalf for a passport to facilitate her return.
Law Minister Md Asaduzzaman said on Saturday (November 14, 2026) that Bangladesh had completed the legal process to secure Ms. Hasina’s return and that the decision now rested with India.

Bangladesh has also linked progress on Ms. Hasina’s extradition to a possible visit to India by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman , saying her return and that of other fugitives sought by Dhaka would help create a conducive environment for the visit.
India has acknowledged receiving Bangladesh’s extradition requests but has not announced a decision.
On Friday (November 13, 2026), Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said in New Delhi that Ms. Hasina’s extradition was a legal matter and would be dealt with accordingly.

Meanwhile, the demonstrators on Sunday (November 15, 2026) pulled down a monument erected to mark the ouster of Ms. Hasina’s government on August 5, 2024, and broke through police barricades to enter several roads in Gopalganj town. Many women activists also joined the protests.

“Our movement on the streets will continue until we can bring former prime minister and Bangabandhu’s (Bangladesh’s founding father Sheikh Mujibur Rahman) daughter Sheikh Hasina back to the country,” Awami League’s Gopalganj district leader Ilyas Haque told a party rally.

articles.title: Fresh unrest in Bangladesh as garment workers protest, block highways for higher wages
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Police and paramilitary personnel used tear gas shells, sound grenades and batons to disperse protesters who blocked the Dhaka-Aricha, Dhaka-Tangail and Dhaka-Mymensingh highways

Authorities in Bangladesh on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) deployed more than 1,000 paramilitary personnel as garment workers staged demonstrations and clashed with police in the industrial belt around Dhaka, demanding higher wages and blocking three major highways.

Police and paramilitary personnel used tear gas shells, sound grenades and batons to disperse protesters who blocked the Dhaka-Aricha, Dhaka-Tangail and Dhaka-Mymensingh highways, disrupting traffic and causing long tailbacks.
The demonstrations are part of weeks of intermittent protests that began in late October across Bangladesh's major garment-producing areas.
The workers have been demanding an increase in the minimum monthly wage from the existing Tk 12,500 ($100) to Tk 30,000 ($240), citing rising costs of food, housing, transport and healthcare.

Bangladesh is the world's second-largest garment exporter after China. The sector employs more than four million workers and accounts for more than 80% of the country's export earnings, with prolonged disruption threatening production schedules, international buyers' confidence and global apparel supply chains.
In a dilemma: On Sheikh Hasina and India-Bangladesh ties

The paramilitary Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) said it had deployed 42 platoons of personnel in the industrial hubs of Ashulia, Gazipur and Narayanganj. Officials said the personnel were also using drones to maintain surveillance over readymade garment factory workers.

Police said two of the three highways had been cleared, but intermittent blockades continued to cause heavy traffic congestion on the Dhaka-Mymensingh highway. "We are working to clear the highways and disperse the protesters," a police spokesperson said.

The industrial unrest also affected factory operations. Police said at least 37 garment factories across the industrial belt were declared closed on Tuesday, while dozens more temporarily suspended production after workers left their workplaces to join demonstrations.

In Dhaka, garment workers gathered in the Darus Salam and Shah Ali police station areas of Mirpur on Tuesday morning and attempted to move towards the Mirpur-10 roundabout, the Prothom Alo newspaper reported.
Police stopped them and later fired sound grenades to disperse the crowd at around 10.30 a.m. local time, Mirpur police station Officer-in-Charge Hafizur Rahman said, according to the report.

In Savar, workers blocked the Dhaka-Aricha Highway in the Fulbaria area around 11 a.m. local time, disrupting traffic in both directions. The blockade continued until around 11.50 a.m., causing long tailbacks and inconvenience to commuters, the Dhaka Tribune newspaper reported.

articles.title: U.S. blocks China’s remote access to AI chips after Nvidia scandal; China slams move
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Nvidia’s provision of chips to companies running data centres in Southeast Asia has come under the spotlight amid questions surrounding founder Jensen Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang, the CEO of one such Singapore-based company, Megaspeed

The United States has announced new regulations aimed at curbing Chinese firms’ remote access to advanced AI chips through data centres in third party countries, coming amid the scandal surrounding chipmaker Nvidia. Beijing on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) slammed the new restrictions, accusing Washington of “abusing export control measures”.

Nvidia’s provision of chips to companies running data centres in Southeast Asia has come under the spotlight amid questions surrounding founder Jensen Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang , the CEO of one such Singapore-based company, Megaspeed . With Nvidia barred from selling its most advanced chips in China, many Chinese companies instead sought access to its technology through data centres in countries such as Malaysia.

The U.S. Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) announced an interim final rule (IFR) “to address remote access” to advanced AI chips and servers, saying it was “designed to ensure that existing restrictions on access to sensitive American technology cannot be circumvented through remote computing arrangements involving data centres in third countries.”

The new rule was announced days before President Donald Trump’s arrival in Shenzhen for meetings with President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the November 18-19 APEC Summit, which will also see a rare trilateral leaders’ summit along with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

The rule states that in addition to the current license requirements for advanced semiconductors, a license will be required “to export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) advanced semiconductors to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, or Brazil”, which it named as “countries which present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion.”

China hit out at the moves, calling it “yet another case of the U.S. overstretching the concept of national security, and abusing export control measures to interfere in normal trade and tech cooperation between China and other countries and go after China’s high-tech industry.”

“Such typical economic coercion and long-arm jurisdiction run counter to the common understandings between the two countries, harm the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese companies, and disrupt global supply chains,” Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said. “China will do what is necessary to firmly safeguard its legitimate and lawful rights and interests.”

articles.title: ASEAN Summit LIVE updates: Quad is a ‘trusted partnership’ delivering solutions, says PM Modi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: In the first Quad Summit since 2024, PM Modi is expected to meet U.S. President Trump, Japanese PM Takaichi and Australian PM Albanese

The Quad grouping, following its meeting in Manila, announced the ‘Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration’ which is “ a new initiative to enhance information sharing and maritime domain awareness”
“In 2027, our respective P-8 and P-3C patrol aircraft are scheduled to fly in a maritime exercise for the first time in a Quad context, making our seas safer,” the statement added.
In a joint press release following the Quad meeting in Manila, the group said that it “affirms the importance of the AI Accelerator, announced by our Foreign Ministers in Atlanta.”
“The Accelerator is intended to coordinate and fund efforts to support trusted AI access, deployment, and technical assistance across the Indo-Pacific,” it added.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi discussed ways to strengthen cooperation and exchanged views on regional and global developments with his counterparts from Singapore and Thailand in separate bilateral meetings in the Philippines.

Mr. Modi, who arrived in Manila on Monday to attend the ASEAN-India Summit and East Asia Summit, met Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong and Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul on the sidelines of the two summits.
PM Modi, at the Quad meeting in Manila, announced that the inaugural Quad Business Leaders Forum will be hosted in Mumbai in 2027, the Ministry of External Affairs said.

The Ministry of External Affairs said that at the Quad meeting, PM Modi “reaffirmed India’s commitment to a constructive and reliable Quad partnership, advancing peace, prosperity and resilience in the Indo-Pacific through cooperation in maritime security, economic security, critical technologies and disaster response.”

U.S. President Donald Trump confirmed four key outcomes of the Quad leaders’ meeting in Manila, covering economic cooperation, artificial intelligence, maritime security and cybersecurity, as leaders of India, the United States, Japan and Australia gathered for the high-level engagement.
The four outcomes include the Quad Business Leaders’ Forum, Super Intelligence Accelerator, Maritime Intelligence Sharing Corporation and Quad cybersecurity intelligence-sharing cooperation.

Addressing the leaders, Trump highlighted the growing importance of the four-nation grouping and announced initiatives to strengthen commercial ties, advance superintelligence and enhance maritime cooperation.

Highlighting their strategic importance, he described the four countries as “the four corners of a free, open, stable, and prosperous Indo-Pacific”, adding that they coordinated closely on regional security, economic security and diplomacy.
