articles.title: What is ‘food is medicine’? – 2 experts explain this decades-old approach to healthcare that is taking on new life
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Access to healthy food would be considered as essential as medications for patients with chronic illness

Mountains of scientific evidence support both the negative and positive effects of our eating habits on our health . Research shows that a healthy diet can help those suffering from chronic health conditions like Type 2 diabetes , heart disease and high blood pressure .

This is where “food is medicine” comes in. Food is medicine, also known as “food as medicine” and “food prescriptions,” is a movement dedicated to providing healthy food – fruits, vegetables and sometimes healthy proteins – based on a clinician’s prescription in order to prevent, manage or treat specific clinical conditions .
Prescribing food to patients is intended to convey that food is just as important as medication for health and wellness.

As researchers whose work focuses on food access and health in rural communities, we have firsthand experience running food is medicine programs in our local area in northern Mississippi. This experience has shown us the benefits and limitations of these programs in our community.

Food is medicine programs can be delivered through curated food boxes, grocery vouchers and medically tailored meals. Most programs are collaborations between nonprofit organizations, health clinics and healthcare providers. The goal of food is medicine is to improve patient health, especially for those with chronic conditions, while reducing healthcare costs.

Increasingly, food is medicine programs have become lifelines for people with food insecurity. In 2024, more than 47 million Americans, including 7.3 million children, lived in food-insecure households – meaning they were at some point uncertain of having, or did not have, enough food for everyone in the household.

Internationally, the number of people experiencing hunger rises to roughly 673 million . Rural populations are more likely to be food insecure due to the loss of local grocery stores and distance from urban centers. Unlike a food bank, food is medicine programs provide only healthy foods, which are often curated by a dietitian, to optimize patient health.

Though food is medicine isn’t formally connected to the Make American Healthy Again movement , U.S. Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. has brought new energy and attention to the concept. In January 2026, the second Trump administration launched a campaign encouraging Americans to “ Eat Real Food .”

But the food is medicine movement actually began more than 60 years ago. One of the early providers who prescribed food as medicine was civil rights activist and multiple Nobel Peace Prize winner Dr. Jack Geiger . In the 1960s, he co-founded community health centers in South Boston and the Mississippi Delta.
When government officials chastised him for prescribing food to patients in the Delta, Geiger responded, “The last time I looked at my textbooks, the most specific therapy for malnutrition was food.”
Since then, thousands of community organizations like Community Servings and Project Open Hand have provided healthy food to vulnerable community members.

In 2023, the president of the American Heart Association convened an advisory group of researchers and physicians to review current food is medicine research and suggest next steps for work in this area. This advisory has suggested that these programs could help prevent or manage chronic conditions, saving the U.S. healthcare system an estimated US$4.3 trillion annually .

articles.title: Diabetes linked with 53% higher risk of Alzheimer's, review finds
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: While many earlier reviews combined different types of diabetes or dementia, this review focused specifically on type 2 diabetes and Alzheimer's disease and estimated how often new cases occurred
People with diabetes could be at a 53% higher risk of Alzheimer's disease, compared to those living without the metabolic disorder, a review of studies has found.

Researchers, led by those from Australia's Curtin University, conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of 40 studies. They found that if 1,000 people living with type 2 diabetes were followed for a year, an estimaated average of 4.7 would develop Alzheimer's disease, a neurodegenerative disorder in which memory and thought processes steadily decline with age.
Cognitive risk prevention should be integrated into diabetes care, they said.

"Individuals with T2D (type 2 diabetes) experienced approximately five AD (Alzheimer's disease) cases per 1,000 person-years and a 53 per cent higher risk of AD, supporting the rationale for integrating cognitive risk prevention into diabetes care," the authors wrote in the study published in the journal Alzheimer's Research and Therapy.

Study author Emmanuel Adewuyi, an investigator fellow at Curtin University's school of population health, said the review was important as it quantifies the relative risk and incidence of Alzheimer's in people living with type 2 diabetes.

"While many earlier reviews combined different types of diabetes or dementia, this review focused specifically on type 2 diabetes and Alzheimer's disease and estimated how often new cases occurred," Adewuyi said.

"Relative risk tells us how two groups compare, while incidence tells us how often new cases occur: putting those numbers together gives us a clearer picture of the burden of Alzheimer's disease among people living with type 2 diabetes," the author said.

Databases including MEDLINE, CINAHL and Embase were searched from for publications since inception until April 2026. Forty studies, involving 27,102,559 data points, and looking at the incidence of Alzheimer's disease among people with diabetes or link between the two disorders were analysed.

articles.title: 91% of studies in India in last 5 decades linked air pollution to health effects: Analysis
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Studies examined a range of air pollutants, with 45 investigating both particulate matter and gaseous pollutants. PM2.5 was examined in 32 studies, PM10 alone in four, and both PM10 and PM2.5 in 16

An analysis of more than 180 epidemiological studies examining the health impacts of air pollution across India has found that over 91% of them reported at least one adverse health association with air pollution exposure.

These studies, published between 1975 and 2025, also noted that health impacts extend beyond respiratory diseases to cardiovascular diseases, diabetes, pregnancy complications, impaired child growth, tumours, blood disorders, mental and neurocognitive disorders, among others.

The analysis, released on Friday, was done by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA), an independent research organisation focused on revealing the trends, causes, and health impacts, as well as the solutions, to air pollution.

Notably, out of 180 studies, only 40 examined air pollution's impact on rural populations, of which 38 reported at least one adverse health association, indicating that air pollution's health impacts are not confined to urban areas.

Further, most studies were conducted on Delhi (26) to examine the link between health and air pollution. The national capital was followed by Punjab with 13 studies, Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh with 11 each, West Bengal with 10, Tamil Nadu with nine, Karnataka with eight and Telangana with seven, the report said.

In a statement, CREA analyst Manoj Kumar said, "The findings highlight the need to move beyond a city-centric approach and explicitly include rural areas through a regional, airshed-based approach in the next phase of National Clean Air Programme (NCAP 2.0)."
Studies examined a range of air pollutants, with 45 investigating both particulate matter and gaseous pollutants. PM2.5 was examined in 32 studies, PM10 alone in four, and both PM10 and PM2.5 in 16.

Among studies examining gaseous pollutants, statistically significant adverse health associations were reported for increased mortality, acute respiratory hospital and emergency visits, asthma-related hospital admissions, and impaired lung function.

Beyond their direct health effects, gaseous pollutants such as SOx and NOx also contribute to secondary PM2.5 formation by undergoing atmospheric chemical reactions to form sulphate and nitrate particles, respectively.

Kumar said, "Air pollution mitigation must adopt a multipollutant approach, addressing gaseous precursors that contribute to secondary PM2.5 and ground-level ozone formation. This requires emission reductions at major sources, including industries, power plants, residential cooking, and other combustion activities."

These studies, published between 1975 and 2025, also noted that health impacts extend beyond respiratory diseases to cardiovascular diseases, diabetes, pregnancy complications, impaired child growth, tumours, blood disorders, mental and neurocognitive disorders, among others.

The analysis, released on Friday, was done by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA), an independent research organisation focused on revealing the trends, causes, and health impacts, as well as the solutions, to air pollution.

Notably, out of 180 studies, only 40 examined air pollution's impact on rural populations, of which 38 reported at least one adverse health association, indicating that air pollution's health impacts are not confined to urban areas.

Further, most studies were conducted on Delhi (26) to examine the link between health and air pollution. The national capital was followed by Punjab with 13 studies, Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh with 11 each, West Bengal with 10, Tamil Nadu with nine, Karnataka with eight and Telangana with seven, the report said.

In a statement, CREA analyst Manoj Kumar said, "The findings highlight the need to move beyond a city-centric approach and explicitly include rural areas through a regional, airshed-based approach in the next phase of National Clean Air Programme (NCAP 2.0)."

Studies examined a range of air pollutants, with 45 investigating both particulate matter and gaseous pollutants. PM2.5 was examined in 32 studies, PM10 alone in four, and both PM10 and PM2.5 in 16.

Among studies examining gaseous pollutants, statistically significant adverse health associations were reported for increased mortality, acute respiratory hospital and emergency visits, asthma-related hospital admissions, and impaired lung function.

Beyond their direct health effects, gaseous pollutants such as SOx and NOx also contribute to secondary PM2.5 formation by undergoing atmospheric chemical reactions to form sulphate and nitrate particles, respectively.

Kumar said, "Air pollution mitigation must adopt a multipollutant approach, addressing gaseous precursors that contribute to secondary PM2.5 and ground-level ozone formation. This requires emission reductions at major sources, including industries, power plants, residential cooking, and other combustion activities."

articles.title: COP31: Experts flag extreme heat risks to pregnant women, call for targeted adaptation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Studies show that exposure to extreme heat can affect pregnant women's health, pregnancy outcomes and the health of newborns

Exposure to extreme heat during pregnancy can lead to severe outcomes, including preterm birth, stillbirth and congenital abnormalities in newborns, prompting experts at the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) to highlight maternal health risks and call for targeted adaptation strategies.

The issue comes into focus as countries at COP31 prepare to discuss progress towards the Global Goal on Adaptation, a framework to help nations develop key adaptation measures, including those needed to address the health impacts of climate change.
However, translating growing recognition of climate-related health risks into action remains a challenge, particularly in the absence of adequate financial support.
According to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), only about one per cent of formal climate finance under its financial mechanism is currently directed towards health.
The broader issue of adaptation finance for developing nations is also expected to feature prominently in discussions in the coming days.

Speaking to PTI on the sidelines of COP31, Alan Dangour, Director of Climate and Health at the Wellcome Trust, said the foundation is seeking to highlight the evidence of heat-related impacts on pregnant women through three key areas -- elevating the issues as a risk for women, developing guidelines and preparing health systems.

“We have three key points: recognising that pregnant women are a particularly vulnerable group when it comes to climate-driven extreme heat, developing guidelines to help nurses, midwives and doctors respond to the challenges pregnant women face during heatwaves, and prepare health systems for a new world shaped by climate change, and identify the most vulnerable people so they are protected,” Dangour said.
He said pregnant women were not always recognised as a particularly vulnerable group and stressed that health systems must specifically account for their needs and risks during heatwaves.

“At the moment they are not recognised as such, and they need to be included in clinical guidelines. When it comes to data, we are keen that countries record the impacts of climate change on pregnant women and then work out how their guidelines and processes can protect them,” he said.
“That evidence is important because we can see what works and what doesn’t in different parts of the world, and share that knowledge,” he said.

Former World Health Organisation (WHO) chief scientist Soumya Swaminathan stressed the importance of highlighting the issue at COP31, saying the health impacts of climate change were already being felt and required immediate action.

“It is good that for the last three COPs or so we have had a day focused on health and climate, because everyone is increasingly recognising that the health impacts of climate change are already happening and need immediate action. They are also hitting certain vulnerable groups disproportionately, and pregnant women are one of them,” Swaminathan told PTI.

articles.title: Health Wrap Episode 59 discusses living with diabetes, approaches to diabetes care and more
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The episode discusses the everyday realities of living with diabetes, experiences of older adults who have managed the condition over several years, and practical approaches to diabetes management, including diet, physical activity and blood glucose monitoring
The 59th episode of Health Wrap by The Hindu, marking World Diabetes Day, explores the everyday realities of living with diabetes and approaches to managing the condition over time.

Ramya Kannan, Health Editor, The Hindu, speaks to individuals living with diabetes, including older adults who share their experiences of managing the condition over several years. Their experiences offer perspectives on living with diabetes and the importance of sustained management.
The episode also features a discussion with Dr. V. Mohan, Chairman and Chief of Diabetology, Dr. Mohan’s Diabetes Specialities Centre, Chennai, on practical approaches to diabetes care.

The discussion looks at the role of dietary habits and food choices in diabetes management, the importance of regular physical activity and exercise, and blood glucose monitoring. It also examines how sustainable changes to everyday food and activity routines can support long-term management of the condition.

The episode discusses practical measures that people living with diabetes can incorporate into their daily lives, the importance of consistent approaches to care, and how genetic predisposition and environmental factors influence the development and management of diabetes. It also explores longevity and living well with diabetes over the years.
The episode can also be viewed on The Hindu health page along with the full playlist of The Health Wrap

articles.title: NASA's Voyager 1 closes in on a light-day in interstellar space for new distance record
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: NASA is looking at another 18,000 years before the spacecraft achieves a full light-year and more than double that before it comes near another star
NASA's Voyager 1 is about to become humanity's first object to reach one light-day from Earth as it pushes ever deeper into interstellar space.
That's a mind-blowing distance of more than 26 billion kilometres for the spacecraft launched 49 years ago.

When Voyager 1 reaches that remarkable milestone on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), its radio signals will take precisely 24 hours travelling at the speed of light to reach Earth — in other words, one light-day.
NASA is looking at another 18,000 years before the spacecraft achieves a full light-year and more than double that before it comes near another star.
Project manager Suzanne Dodd sees Voyager 1 as Earth's ambassador hurtling between stars while providing a “sense of wonder” on the home front.
“It's a national treasure,” she told The Associated Press . “Really extraordinary.”

To celebrate this moment, NASA is urging people from all corners to grab their phone or a flashlight to create a wave of golden light after sunset on Tuesday (November 17), using Morse code to spell the letters V-G-R, Voyager's call sign, into the night sky.

Despite sporadic problems typical of old age, Voyager 1 and its twin Voyager 2 continue to send back science and engineering data as they zoom toward different points in space at 61,000 kph. Although launched two weeks before its sibling in 1977, Voyager 2 won't reach the one light-day mark until 2035.

Voyager 1 swept past Jupiter and Saturn to scientists' delight in 1979 and 1980, respectively, before exiting the solar system. It reached what NASA defines as interstellar space — the expansive region between star systems — in 2012. Voyager 2 visited those two planets plus Uranus and Neptune, also sending back stunning photos, before entering interstellar space in 2018.

Almost every day, the Voyagers beam back details about their never-before-explored environment: the strength and direction of the magnetic field as well as tidbits about the surrounding pressure, dust and galactic cosmic rays. They're a bit like weather satellites, according to Dodd, who's worked with the Voyagers since 1984.

The skeleton flight control team at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Pasadena, California, sends commands about once a week. The operation ramps up when spacecraft problems arise, with help sometimes coming from a couple of retirees who once worked on the project.

In September, controllers completed the latest power-conserving effort for the plutonium-powered spacecraft, then in October briefly lost contact with it. They're still trying to figure out why communication was disrupted.

articles.title: TMC government considered only Muslims as minority: Bengal CM
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: “Minority does not mean a particular community. Sikhs, Buddhists and Jains are also [religious] minorities. The previous TMC government considered only Muslims as a minority,” says West Bengal CM

West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Sunday (November 15, 2026) alleged that the previous TMC government had considered only Muslims as a minority, asserting that Sikhs, Buddhists and Jains are also religious minorities.
He visited the Gurdwara Bara Sikh Sangat at the city's trading hub, Burrabazar, and participated in a procession of the Sikh community in the area.

"Minority does not mean a particular community. Sikhs, Buddhists and Jains are also [religious] minorities. The previous TMC government considered only Muslims as a minority," the Chief Minister told reporters after greeting the members of the Sikh community in the gurdwara.
"They [Sikhs] are the truest patriots," the Chief Minister said.
Earlier, Mr. Adhikari had repeatedly accused the Mamata Banerjee -led government of indulging in the appeasement of the Muslim community to garner their support in the elections.

articles.title: Cyclone Akvan to move towards Andhra coast by November 19, rainfall expected in Tamil Nadu, Bengal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The cyclone is expected to bring rains to Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, and West Bengal.

A depression over the southeast and adjoining southwest Bay of Bengal is likely to strengthen into a severe cyclonic storm by November 17, the meteorological department said on Sunday (November 15, 2026).

Cyclone Akvan is expected to cause rains in north coastal districts in Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal area, it said. The department announced that the cycline is expected to move towards the Andhra Pradesh coast around November 19.

The Regional Meteorological Centre issued a Nowcast alert at 1 p.m. in Tamilnadu, valid till 4 p.m. for light to moderate rainfall at isolated places over Cuddalore, Chengalpattu, Mayiladuthurai, Nagappattinam, Pudukkottai, Thanjavur, Thiruvarur and Viluppuram districts and Karaikal and Puducherry.

According to the latest weather report, Saturday's (November 14) well-marked low-pressure area over the southeast Bay of Bengal moved northwestward, intensified into a depression and lay centred at 5:30 a.m. today. It is very likely to continue to move northwestward, intensify further into a cyclonic storm over the central parts of the south and adjoining west-central Bay of Bengal on November, 16 and into a severe cyclonic storm on November 17.

The data further added that in addition to northern Tamil Nadu districts, moderate rain at isolated places is likely to occur over western ghat and southern districts of the State from Monday (November 16).

The Depression over Southeast & adjoining Southwest Bay of Bengal moved nearly northwards with the speed of 10 kmph during past 03 hours and lay centered at 0830 hours IST of today, the 15th November, 2026 over the same region, near Latitude 9.3°N and Longitude 86.9°E, about 630 km east of Trincomalee (Sri Lanka), 690km west-southwest of Sri Vijaya Puram (Andaman & Nicobar Islands), 840 km east-southeast of Chennai (Tamil Nadu), 1010 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh) and 1130 km south-southeast of Gopalpur (Odisha). It is very likely to move north-northwestwards, intensify further into a Cyclonic Storm over the central parts of south & adjoining westcentral Bay of Bengal on 16th November and into a Severe Cyclonic Storm over westcentral Bay of Bengal on 17th November, 2026. Thereafter, it is likely to intensify further and move northwestwards towards Andhra Pradesh coast during subsequent 2 days.
According to the bulletin, during the last 24 hours ending at 8:30 a.m. on Sunday (November 15), rainfall occurred in several districts, including Chengalpattu, Chennai, Kancheepuram and Kanyakumari.

The IMD alerted that the cyclone will bring heavy rain to some districts of West Bengal from November 19 to 21. It will bring heavy rain to the coastal districts of South 24 Parganas and Purba Medinipur from November 19 to 21, the department said. A downpour is also likely in the southern districts of Howrah, Paschim Medinipur and Jhargram on November 20 and 21.
According to the IMD, thunderstorms, accompanied with winds up to 40 kmph in Kolkata and most districts of Gangetic West Bengal is also likely.
A nip in the air over South Bengal is likely to dissipate as day and night temperatures will rise by two to three degrees Celsius from November 18, it said.

🏛️ National & Polity 📅 15 Nov 2026 • IN-APP NEWSPAPER PRINT EDITION

Cyclone Akvan to move towards Andhra coast by November 19, rainfall expected in Tamil Nadu, Bengal

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes

The cyclone is expected to bring rains to Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, and West Bengal.

A depression over the southeast and adjoining southwest Bay of Bengal is likely to strengthen into a severe cyclonic storm by November 17, the meteorological department said on Sunday (November 15, 2026).

Cyclone Akvan is expected to cause rains in north coastal districts in Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal area, it said. The department announced that the cycline is expected to move towards the Andhra Pradesh coast around November 19.

The Regional Meteorological Centre issued a Nowcast alert at 1 p.m. in Tamilnadu, valid till 4 p.m. for light to moderate rainfall at isolated places over Cuddalore, Chengalpattu, Mayiladuthurai, Nagappattinam, Pudukkottai, Thanjavur, Thiruvarur and Viluppuram districts and Karaikal and Puducherry.

According to the latest weather report, Saturday's (November 14) well-marked low-pressure area over the southeast Bay of Bengal moved northwestward, intensified into a depression and lay centred at 5:30 a.m. today. It is very likely to continue to move northwestward, intensify further into a cyclonic storm over the central parts of the south and adjoining west-central Bay of Bengal on November, 16 and into a severe cyclonic storm on November 17.

The data further added that in addition to northern Tamil Nadu districts, moderate rain at isolated places is likely to occur over western ghat and southern districts of the State from Monday (November 16).

The Depression over Southeast & adjoining Southwest Bay of Bengal moved nearly northwards with the speed of 10 kmph during past 03 hours and lay centered at 0830 hours IST of today, the 15th November, 2026 over the same region, near Latitude 9.3°N and Longitude 86.9°E, about 630 km east of Trincomalee (Sri Lanka), 690km west-southwest of Sri Vijaya Puram (Andaman & Nicobar Islands), 840 km east-southeast of Chennai (Tamil Nadu), 1010 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh) and 1130 km south-southeast of Gopalpur (Odisha). It is very likely to move north-northwestwards, intensify further into a Cyclonic Storm over the central parts of south & adjoining westcentral Bay of Bengal on 16th November and into a Severe Cyclonic Storm over westcentral Bay of Bengal on 17th November, 2026. Thereafter, it is likely to intensify further and move northwestwards towards Andhra Pradesh coast during subsequent 2 days.

According to the bulletin, during the last 24 hours ending at 8:30 a.m. on Sunday (November 15), rainfall occurred in several districts, including Chengalpattu, Chennai, Kancheepuram and Kanyakumari.

The IMD alerted that the cyclone will bring heavy rain to some districts of West Bengal from November 19 to 21. It will bring heavy rain to the coastal districts of South 24 Parganas and Purba Medinipur from November 19 to 21, the department said. A downpour is also likely in the southern districts of Howrah, Paschim Medinipur and Jhargram on November 20 and 21.

According to the IMD, thunderstorms, accompanied with winds up to 40 kmph in Kolkata and most districts of Gangetic West Bengal is also likely.

A nip in the air over South Bengal is likely to dissipate as day and night temperatures will rise by two to three degrees Celsius from November 18, it said.

articles.title: Mekedatu is Karnataka’s right, we will build dam and release Tamil Nadu’s share of water: D.K. Shivakumar
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Karnataka Chief Minister invites Tamil Nadu delegation to visit project site and understand its benefits rather than oppose it

Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Saturday (November 14) asserted that Karnataka will go ahead with the Mekedatu balancing reservoir project , describing it as the State’s right and duty, while assuring that Tamil Nadu would receive its stipulated share of Cauvery water.

Responding to opposition to the project from leaders in Tamil Nadu, including State Congress president Manickam Tagore, Mr. Shivakumar said the neighbouring State should send a delegation to Karnataka to understand the project’s benefits rather than oppose it.

“Anyone is free to oppose it, but Tamil Nadu must recognise that this is our State and our right. If they wish, let them send a delegation. I am prepared to take them to the dam site and explain the project,” he told presspersons.

He said Karnataka would respect Tamil Nadu’s entitlement of 177 tmcft of Cauvery water as stipulated by the Supreme Court. “We will build the dam and ensure that they receive their share. Protecting Karnataka’s water rights while ensuring that Tamil Nadu gets its due share is our responsibility. We will not back down when it comes to safeguarding the interests of our State,” he said.
Describing the opposition to the project as politically motivated, he said the issue should be viewed in the context of the law and the Supreme Court’s directions rather than political rivalry.
“This is not a political matter. Everyone must respect the law of the land and abide by the Supreme Court’s order. Receiving 177 tmcft of water is Tamil Nadu’s right, and we will honour it,” he said.

Mr. Shivakumar said the State had sought the necessary forest and environmental clearances from the Centre and was preparing the required documents. All political parties in Karnataka had supported the project, he said, pointing out that the government was ready to take it forward once the clearances were obtained. The Centre’s requirement to provide compensatory land for the forest area that would be submerged was among the issues to be addressed.

In his interaction with Prime Minister Narendra Modi during the latter’s visit to Karnataka on Friday (November 13), Mr. Shivakumar said political differences should not come in the way of development.
“Let us compete in politics, but cooperate on development. Securing the Centre’s support for the State’s growth is our responsibility,” he said.

He said he had also urged the Centre to reject the Kasturirangan report and sought equal participation by the Centre and the State in funding Bengaluru metro projects. He had proposed the formation of a technical committee to oversee the projects and sought faster clearances for pending proposals. The State aimed to expand the metro network to 500 km in future phases, he said.

On the pending power dues raised during the Suvarna Soudha session, Mr. Shivakumar said the government’s subsidy burden towards electricity supplied to farmers’ irrigation pumpsets had increased from about ₹20,000 crore to ₹30,000 crore.

He attributed the increase to higher power consumption during drought conditions and the use of lift irrigation schemes to fill tanks, among other factors. The government would address the issue and resolve the pending matters, he said.

articles.title: Dhinakaran, Vasan urge Vijay to protect interests of T.N. farmers in Mekedatu issue
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: In a statement, Mr. Dhinakaran accused Mr. Vijay of failing to discharge his responsibility to protect farmers’ livelihoods for the sake of retaining power, alleging this had emboldened D.K. Shivakumar to persist with the Mekedatu project

AMMK founder T.T.V. Dhinakaran on Sunday (November 15, 2026) accused Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay of shedding crocodile tears over the Mekedatu dam issue and said the latter had to choose between his party’s alliance with the Congress and the livelihoods of Tamil Nadu farmers.

In a statement, Mr. Dhinakaran accused Mr. Vijay of failing to discharge his responsibility to protect farmers’ livelihoods for the sake of retaining power, alleging this had emboldened Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar to persist with the Mekedatu project.

Condemning Mr. Shivakumar’s remarks on constructing the dam across the Cauvery, Mr. Dhinakaran urged Mr. Vijay to exert political pressure through the Congress leadership to stop the project, warning failure to do so would amount to a betrayal of Tamil Nadu farmers.

Tamil Maanila Congress (Moopanar) leader G.K. Vasan also criticised Mr. Shivakumar’s remarks on constructing the Mekedatu dam, stating his demand for the Centre’s support and his interpretation of the Supreme Court’s verdict were unacceptable.

In a statement, Mr. Vasan said Karnataka’s efforts to construct the dam amounted to an infringement of Tamil Nadu’s rights. The Mekedatu water issue was not merely a crop-related concern but a matter of survival for farmers in Tamil Nadu, he said.
Amma Makkal Munnetra Kazhagam / Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam / Indian National Congress / Tamil Maanila Congress

articles.title: Statewide vaccination drive to protect children aged 10 and 16 against tetanus and diphtheria
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Children receive Pentavalent vaccines when very young as part of the immunisation programme, and the TD vaccine is administered to provide additional protection
A vaccination drive will be held across the State from December 3 to 5 to protect children against diphtheria and tetanus, which are potentially life-threatening yet preventable bacterial diseases.

According to a release from the Department of Health, Medical and Family Welfare, the TD (Tetanus-Diphtheria) vaccine will be administered to children who have completed 10 and 16 years of age. The health department aims to cover more than 95% of children in this age bracket during the drive, which will be conducted across government and private schools and intermediate colleges on three days.

Children receive Pentavalent vaccines when very young as part of the immunisation programme, and the TD vaccine is administered to provide additional protection. According to the release, protection during adolescence is also essential, as diphtheria and tetanus are infectious diseases that can cause serious illness and even prove fatal.
Children who have completed 10 years of age should be administered the TD-10 vaccine, while those who have completed 16 years should receive the TD-16 vaccine.

Before the drive begins, ANMs have been directed to prepare a list of government and private schools and intermediate colleges in their jurisdictions and collect details of children eligible for vaccination. They should also identify those who did not attend schools or colleges. They have also been tasked with arranging the required vaccine doses, medical supplies, among other things.

Health and Family Welfare Commissioner and National Health Mission Director K.V.N. Chakradhar Babu directed District Medical and Health Officers, District Immunisation Officers and medical officers working in Primary Health Centres to conduct coordination meetings with the departments of Women and Child Welfare, Education, Minority Welfare, Panchayat Raj and Municipal Administration and Urban Development for the effective implementation of the drive.

Mr. Chakradhar Babu directed district health officials to continuously monitor the drive and inspect vaccination centres to ensure adequate vaccine availability, anaphylaxis kits, and other medical supplies to treat any emergencies.
Once vaccination is completed, digital certificates of the same should be issued to all beneficiaries and the same information should be uploaded on online health portals, the official said.

articles.title: German delegation visits Auroville
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Ambassador also expressed his interest in the founders’ spiritual vision and said he planned to return to Auroville in December

German Ambassador to India Jasper Wieck, accompanied by Michael Hasper, Consul General at the German Consulate General in Chennai, visited the international township of Auroville on Saturday (November 14, 2026).

The delegation was received by officials of the Auroville Foundation, including Officer on Special Duty G. Seetharaman, along with members of the Auroville Town Development Council (ATDC) and the Working Committee.

According to a press note, the centrepiece of the visit was an interactive meeting with the ATDC and the Working Committee, addressed virtually by Jayanti S. Ravi, Secretary of the Auroville Foundation (Ministry of Education, Government of India) and Additional Chief Secretary to the Government of Gujarat.

Foundation officials briefed the delegation on progress under the township’s Galaxy Master Plan, including the 98 per cent completion of the 4.4-km circular Crown Road, which links Auroville’s Residential, Industrial, Cultural and International zones, and upcoming projects such as youth housing, a Civic Anchor Town Hall, the Morning Star Women’s Wellness Center and CIRHU, the Centre for International Research on Human Unity.

They also presented Auroville’s economic life, comprising some 150 production and service units and 700 micro-enterprises, including solar energy initiatives such as Sunlit Future, the Solar Kitchen, and Svaram, its musical instrument research and production centre.

Highlighting the historical and intellectual affinities between India and Germany, particularly Germany’s tradition of Sanskrit and Vedic scholarship, Ms. Ravi proposed a roadmap for Indo-German engagement in Auroville.

The proposals include participation by German authors, poets and artists in the Auroville Literary Festival in December and events at the 12 cultural venues of Bharat Nivas, structured internships and exchange programmes linking German universities with Auroville’s youth and research units, German film screenings at Cinema Paradiso, and collaboration on sports culture and youth training.

The delegation later toured the Matrimandir and its gardens and the Amphitheatre. The Ambassador also expressed his interest in the founders’ spiritual vision and said he planned to return to Auroville in December.

articles.title: Trump administration blames ‘overloaded’ systems for ground stop after FAA lets flights resume
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Thousands of flights and potentially over a million travellers were affected from coast to coast

Trump administration officials said Friday (November 13, 2026) that new technology being added to the nation's air traffic control system overloaded antiquated systems and caused “intermittent” communications and radar gaps, leading to the longest nationwide ground stop in 25 years.
It was lifted Friday (November 13, 2026) night after a five-hour stretch when most flights were not allowed to take off from airports in the United States.

Thousands of flights and potentially over a million travellers were affected from coast to coast. Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin told reporters at the White House that no one was in any danger as more than 3,000 flights were safely landed. But Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy said he could not guarantee it wouldn't happen again.
Mr. Mullin said the FAA was installing “new equipment, new technology” and “it was overwhelming the older system.” There appeared to be no indication of a cyberattack, Mr. Mullin said.

A limited number of domestic flights began departing Friday (November 13, 2026) evening after the ground stop was lifted, but it would likely take days for airlines to fully recover because so many planes and crews were out of position. Officials said they think the system will be back to normal in time to handle the Thanksgiving travel rush.
The nationwide ground stop was the first since January 2023, when a key FAA computer system malfunctioned, and the second since the aftermath of the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks.

Asked whether he could rule out a cyberattack or rogue artificial intelligence incident, Mr. Mullin said: “There's nothing completely certain right now. It doesn't appear that way.” He said there are no “footprints” showing an attack and that it appears to be “mechanically driven,” adding that officials were still looking for the cause.

At least 827 flights had been diverted. As of 7.05 p.m. EST, 670 flights were sent back to the airport from where they originally took off, while 157 were redirected to a different airport, according to Cirium, an aviation analytics company.

The airports where many of the flights ended up being diverted included Washington Dulles International Airport, Los Angeles International Airport, Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport and Nashville International Airport.
Some 11,000 flights carrying more than 1.5 million passengers had been scheduled to take off from airports in the U.S. after 4 p.m. EST.
At the time of the ground stoppage, 3,500 airplanes were in the sky, Mr. Duffy said.
“And last time I looked, we had less than 400 in the airspace,” he said. He said it's going to be slow getting air traffic back to normal.

articles.title: Keralam power purchase row: Opposition Leader Pinarayi Vijayan alleges irregularities in decision to procure 200 MW from VEH Global
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Pinarayi alleges that government decided to purchase power from VEH Global at a relatively high price of ₹11 per unit without inviting bids or securing the approval of the Kerala State Electricity Regulatory Commission

Leader of Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan has alleged that the United Democratic Front (UDF) government decided to purchase electricity from a firm called VEH Global at a relatively high price of ₹11 per unit without inviting bids or securing the approval of the Kerala State Electricity Regulatory Commission (KSERC).

According to the Leader of the Opposition, a supply of 200 MW was secured merely on the strength of an offer made by the firm. The Commission has not yet approved this power purchase, Mr. Vijayan said.
According to him, the government entered into this deal when wind energy costs just ₹3 or ₹4 per unit. The UDF decision entails a huge loss for the exchequer, he said.

Mr. Vijayan also alleged that VEH Global was ineligible to participate in a tender process. According to him, the government issued orders on September 22 allowing power procurement from this firm. The same order mentioned its ineligibility, he said.

Recently, the UDF government’s decision to procure electricity from over-the-counter (OTC) platform GNA Energy allegedly overlooking an offer from the Himachal Pradesh government had sparked a major political row in Keralam.

On Sunday (November 15, 2026), Mr. Vijayan demanded that Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan explain to the people on what basis was the agreement with VEH Global entered into. On the corruption allegations related to the GNA Energy deal, Mr. Satheesan had defended himself saying that no agreement had been inked with GNA. However, in this case, he cannot say so, Mr. Vijayan said.

articles.title: Air India resumes direct flights to New York, Newark after easing of airspace curbs
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Air India has one daily flight to New York and four weekly services to Newark from Delhi. All of them are operated with A350-900 aircraft

Air India on Sunday (November 15, 2026) said it has resumed non-stop flights to New York and Newark from Delhi and Mumbai, following the reopening of a restricted airspace, reducing overall travel time by up to five hours.
From the first week of this month, Air India began operating these direct flights without a stopover, with the airline using Iraq airspace, sources told PTI on November 6.
Air India has one daily flight to New York and four weekly services to Newark from Delhi. All of them are operated with A350-900 aircraft.
From Mumbai, the airline flies daily services to New York and three weekly flights to Newark with Boeing 777-300 ER planes.

With the easing of airspace curbs, Air India on Sunday said the total travel time for each flight on the routes to New York and Newark from Delhi and Mumbai has been cut down by around 5 hours to 17 hours. Previously, the total travel time was around 22 hours due to an en route fuelling stop at Rome (Italy).
This year, the closure of Pakistan airspace and airspace restrictions across parts of West Asia amid regional conflict had significantly impacted flight routings between India and North America.

Subsequently, Air India's flights from Delhi and Mumbai to New York's John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK) and Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR) started operating with a technical stop in Rome for refuelling.
"With airspace restrictions eased, Air India has now resumed non-stop operations on all four India-New York routes," the airline said.
Earlier, the longer routings for these flights through Jordan and Egypt resulted in increased flying hours.
Last month, a senior airline official said there was a big impact due to the airspace restrictions, including due to the West Asia crisis, and the impact was worse than last year.

"The more airspaces are closed, the more southwards flights have to go... the more southwards flights have to go, the more the fuel bill. So, it (airspace curbs) is worse than what we had last year," the official had said.

"With airspace restrictions eased, Air India has now resumed non-stop operations on all four India-New York routes," the airline said.

Earlier, the longer routings for these flights through Jordan and Egypt resulted in increased flying hours.

Last month, a senior airline official said there was a big impact due to the airspace restrictions, including due to the West Asia crisis, and the impact was worse than last year.

"The more airspaces are closed, the more southwards flights have to go... the more southwards flights have to go, the more the fuel bill. So, it (airspace curbs) is worse than what we had last year," the official had said.

articles.title: Tripura Government prioritising socio-economic development of tribals: CM Manik Saha
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Addressing a 'Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas' programme at Chawmanu in Dhalai district, Manik Saha recalled the tribal icon, Birsa Munda’s, contribution to the country's freedom struggle

Tripura Chief Minister Manik Saha on Sunday (November 15, 2026) paid tribute to tribal icon Birsa Munda on his 151st birth anniversary and said his Government has been prioritising the overall socio-economic development of the indigenous people.
Addressing a 'Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas' programme at Chawmanu in Dhalai district, Mr. Saha recalled the tribal icon's contribution to the country's freedom struggle.

“The contribution of indigenous people in the country’s freedom struggle was immense. Birsa Munda had fought the British, showing extreme courage. We must salute his contribution to the freedom struggle on his birth anniversary," the CM said.
Born in 1875 at Ulihatu village in Jharkhand's Khunti district, Birsa Munda is credited with mobilising tribals against colonial rule. He died in British custody at the age of 25 on June 9, 1900.

The birth anniversary of the freedom fighter has been celebrated as Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas since 2021 to honour the contributions of tribal communities, especially in India's freedom struggle, and highlights their important role in preserving the country's heritage and advancing its progress.
"Our Government has been giving priority to the overall socio-economic development of the indigenous people," Mr. Saha said.
On the occasion, four Eklavya Model Residential Schools, fully residential schools for tribal students, were inaugurated in Tripura.

“With today’s inauguration of four Eklavya schools, 16 such schools are made operational in the northeastern state while two more will be opened shortly. The Centre has sanctioned 21 such schools altogether for our State. Over 10,000 students will be able to study in these residential schools once all 21 are made functional in the state," he said.
Mr. Saha said Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Tribal Welfare Minister Jual Oram participated in a programme virtually from Delhi on the occasion of Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas.

On the occasion, Mr. Modi inaugurated and laid the foundation stones for 246 development projects worth around ₹3,000 crore aimed at strengthening education, healthcare, livelihood opportunities and community infrastructure in tribal areas.

Of the 246 projects, 173 were inaugurated, including 38 Eklavya Model Residential Schools for tribal students and 100 Multi-Purpose Centres under the Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN).
The four Eklavya schools were among 38 schools inaugurated by Mr. Modi during the day.

articles.title: Assam Congress writes to PM, seeks enhanced aid for victims of Kaziranga accident
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: In the letter, Debabrata Saikia expressed concern over the deplorable condition of the National Highway-715 stretch and alleged that the authorities' neglect of essential road safety measures was disturbing

Assam Congress leader Debabrata Saikia on Sunday (November 15, 2026) urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to enhance compensation for victims of the Kaziranga minibus-truck collision , provide free treatment to the injured and livelihood assistance to families of the 26 deceased.

In the letter, the former leader of the opposition in the Assembly expressed concern over the deplorable condition of the National Highway-715 stretch and alleged that the authorities' neglect of essential road safety measures was disturbing.

Mr. Saikia demanded a thorough examination of the road's condition, design, maintenance, traffic management and safety arrangements, as well as urgent intervention on highway safety, healthcare and infrastructure of the region.

Appreciating the Prime Minister for announcing financial assistance immediately after the accident, he added that the magnitude of the tragedy demanded enhanced compensation and rehabilitation measures.

Administrative accountability must be fixed while the conduct of the drivers involved must also be investigated, the Congress leader said in the letter while expressing disappointment over the response of Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma, who visited the accident site a day later on Saturday (November 14, 2026).

Mr. Saikia claimed that while Mr. Sarma announced ex gratia and promised a probe into the accident, his remarks had failed to adequately address the grievances of locals about the highway. He also referred to the Chief Minister's reported remarks about a possible medical emergency involving the deceased driver, saying this should not divert attention from potential deficiencies in highway infrastructure.

At least 26 people died, including minors, and 20 others were injured in a head-on collision between a minibus and a container truck near Kaziranga National Park in Assam on Friday (November 13, 2026), officials said. Many of the victims were college students.

The Congress leader further said that Mr. Sarma himself had acknowledged that certain traffic restrictions had previously been relaxed under political pressure, making an independent examination of administrative decisions necessary.

In the letter, he also raised concerns relating to the Kaziranga region, including the NH-715 safety, healthcare facilities, alleged misuse of hospital premises, environmental protection, expansion of the eco-sensitive zone and land acquisitions, among others.

Mr. Saikia sought an increase in total compensation to the next of kin of each deceased to at least ₹20 lakh, inclusive of the ₹9 lakh already announced by the Central and State Governments, with additional assistance for families losing multiple members.

He also sought free medical treatment, rehabilitation and disability compensation for the injured, scholarships for dependent children, and livelihood assistance for families losing their principal earning members.
The Congress leader further asked for a comprehensive independent enquiry into the accident, including the NH-715 condition and compliance with safety standards.

articles.title: Megaspeed says Alice Huang left company in August 2025
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Megaspeed said it conducted "legitimate ‌and lawful business" and ​had retained external legal counsel to ⁠conduct a thorough internal ⁠investigation

Megaspeed said on Sunday (November 15, 2026) ​that Chinese businesswoman Alice ‌Huang , whose ties ​to former ⁠Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang raised U.S. national security ‌concerns, had officially left Megaspeed on ‌August 30, ‌2025, ⁠and had no ⁠current role at the Singapore-based company.
"Megaspeed does not ​comment on ‌Ms. Huang’s personal and private matters," the company added in ‌a statement.
"Megaspeed is ​aware of recent media reports ⁠containing assertions about our business, supply chain ‌and global operations that are not supported by verifiable evidence."
The company said it conducted "legitimate ‌and lawful business" and ​had retained external legal counsel to ⁠conduct a thorough internal ⁠investigation.

Two people were injured after a Copa Airlines passenger plane collided with a UPS cargo aircraft while taxiing on the tarmac at Miami International Airport in the U.S., a media report said.

The incident occurred around 9:15 p.m. on Saturday (November 14, 2026) when the wingtip of a Copa Airlines Boeing 737 struck the nose of a UPS Boeing 767, the CNN report said, citing the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA).
Air traffic controllers had instructed the UPS crew to give way to the Copa aircraft, the FAA said, adding that it was investigating the collision.
According to the report, all 166 passengers and six crew members disembarked, and the Copa aircraft returned to the terminal.
Both persons sustained minor injuries and were treated at the scene, CNN quoted airport communications director Greg Chin as saying.
The Copa flight had arrived from Panama City, while the UPS aircraft was preparing to depart for Bogota, Colombia, the report said.
"Our crew is safe, and we are committed to working with authorities to determine what happened," UPS Airlines said on X.
"The safety of our employees and the public is our highest priority," it added.
Meanwhile, Copa Airlines issued a statement expressing regret over the disruption to passengers.
The incident came a day after a nationwide flight grounding triggered widespread cancellations across the U.S..

articles.title: Fading tetanus and diphtheria immunity: experts explain why the Td shot is important
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Tetanus remains preventable. Bridging the adult booster gap may determine whether India can move from control to elimination of avoidable deaths

Tetanus and diphtheria are two preventable diseases. And still, they surface years after childhood vaccinations. As antibody levels decline over time, especially against diphtheria, could the introduction of the Td vaccine signal a crucial point in closing this long-overlooked gap in adult vaccination and protection?

According to the World Health Organization (WHO), maternal and neonatal tetanus has declined significantly over the past two decades. But thousands of people still die from the disease each year, with newborns being especially at risk, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Diphtheria also continues to cause outbreaks in areas where immunity wanes or vaccine coverage is insufficient.

articles.title: Two held in Rajasthan railway track blast case; police cite Pakistani handler links
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Two people were arrested from Punjab’s Gurdaspur over the November 3 blast in Ramsinghpur, and police say they allegedly acted on instructions from Pakistan-based handlers

Two accused in the November 3, 2026, railway track blast in Ramsinghpur were arrested from Punjab’s Gurdaspur, with preliminary investigation indicating their links with Pakistani handlers, the police said on Sunday (November 15, 2026).
The accused, identified as Mahakdeep Kaur and Devendra Singh, were arrested in a joint operation of the Rajasthan Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) and the Sri Ganganagar police.

According to the police, Ms. Kaur was allegedly in contact with a Pakistani handler identified as Shah and had conspired with her associate to carry out the explosion on railway tracks in the Ramsinghpur police station area.
Two foreign-made pistols, 46 live cartridges and ₹30,000, allegedly received for carrying out the blast, have been recovered from their possession, officials said.
The arrests were made on November 14, 2026, in a joint operation by the Rajasthan ATS and the Sri Ganganagar police, in coordination with Counter Intelligence Punjab and the Gurdaspur police.

Under the direction of Additional Director General of Police (ADGP) Dinesh M.N., a joint team was constituted under Sri Ganganagar Superintendent of Police Harishankar. The team collected inputs from central investigating agencies and analysed technical information and the social media accounts of suspects.

The investigation pointed to the involvement of Ms. Kaur and Devendra Singh, residents of Gurdaspur. A team led by probationary Indian Police Service (IPS) officer Nitin Chaudhary, the investigating officer, and ATS Bikaner unit in-charge Surendra Kumar was subsequently sent to Punjab.

The Rajasthan team shared intelligence and technical inputs with Counter Intelligence Punjab and Gurdaspur Senior Superintendent of Police Aditya before the two suspects were detained and arrested following questioning.

Preliminary investigation has revealed that Ms. Kaur’s husband, Karanveer Singh, had earlier been arrested in Punjab in a narcotics smuggling case. Following his arrest, she allegedly came in contact with Pakistan-based handlers, the police said.

Investigators have identified a Pakistani handler named Shah and another person referred to as ‘Chacha’ as allegedly directing the accused to execute the blast. The police said ‘Chacha’ was believed to have links with the Directorate for Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI), Pakistan’s spy agency.

According to the investigation, the accused had initially planned to carry out an explosion on October 6, 2026, in the Ramsinghpur area, but could not do so because an explosive device was not available.
A timer bomb allegedly provided by Shah was subsequently placed on the railway track on October 12 and 13, but failed to explode due to technical defects, the police said.

articles.title: BJP attacks Congress’s absence at Birsa Munda tribute event in Parliament complex
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The BJP terms the Opposition leader’s absence at the ‘Janjatiya Gaurav Divas’ event commemorating the birth anniversary of tribal leader and freedom fighter Birsa Munda as hypocrisy

The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Sunday (November 15, 2026) criticised the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, for not attending an event commemorating the 151st birth anniversary of tribal leader Bisra Munda, held at the Parliament complex here, while having attended what the party termed an “anti-Bharat summit” in Hyderabad.

President Droupadi Murmu, Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla and Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday paid floral tributes to Birsa Munda in the Parliament complex on the occasion of the freedom fighter’s 151st birth anniversary, celebrated as ‘Janjatiya Gaurav Divas’.

The BJP’s national convenor Ashish Usha Agarwal posted a picture from the event on social media platform X and questioned Mr. Gandhi’s absence. “Rahul Gandhi and the Congress never miss an opportunity to claim that they are the voice of Adivasis and champions of tribal rights. But where were they today? On Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas, the birth anniversary of Dharti Aaba Bhagwan Birsa Munda, Rahul Gandhi, the Leader of Opposition, and the Congress were conspicuous by their absence from the parliamentary tribute programme,” Mr. Agarwal said in his post.

“Instead, Rahul Gandhi was busy attending the anti-Bharat Summit in Hyderabad, an event whose proceedings have raised serious questions about its political agenda and discourse on India’s democracy,” Mr. Agarwal added.

He was referring to the ‘Bharat Summit’, an Congress initiative backed by the Telangana government. The BJP has alleged that the invitees included individuals with links to George Soros-backed networks, who were known to make anti-India statements.
“The question to Rahul Gandhi and Congress is simple: Where were the so-called champions of Adivasi rights when the nation was paying tribute to its greatest tribal icon?” Mr. Agarwal said.

The BJP’s Scheduled Tribe Morcha chief Mannalal Rawat also criticised Mr. Gandhi’s absence from the function at the Parliament complex, stating that it exposed the Congress’s hypocrisy. “They keep talking about Adivasis but are nowhere to be found on the day we honour Bhagwan Birsa Munda, who is not just an embodiment of the aspirations of the Adivasis but also a national leader. People are watching everything. This exposes the hypocrisy of the Congress and its leaders on the Adivasi community,” Mr. Rawat said.

articles.title: Tribals suffered most due to Maoist violence, even denied right to vote: PM Modi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Prime Minister Narendra Modi virtually addressing a 'Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas' programme at Gadchiroli in Maharashtra, marking the 151st birth anniversary of tribal freedom fighter Birsa Munda

Tribal communities suffered the most due to Maoist violence and were even denied the right to vote in the Maoist-affected areas, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said on Sunday (November 15, 2026), accusing previous governments of leaving them to fend for themselves.

Virtually addressing a 'Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas' programme at Gadchiroli in Maharashtra, marking the 151st birth anniversary of tribal freedom fighter Birsa Munda, Mr. Modi said the previous governments remained silent when Maoists forcibly took away children and abducted young tribal women.
“Naxals denied the tribal communities voting rights but the previous governments remained mute spectators," Mr. Modi said.
However, the situation has since changed with the elimination of Maoist violence, and tribal mothers and sisters are now blessing the government as they feel secure, Mr. Modi said.
Children whose childhood was affected by violence are now getting opportunities for education and employment, he added.
Mr. Modi also said that nearly 50 crore people have come out of extreme poverty over the past 12-13 years, terming it one of India's biggest achievements since Independence.
Citing a World Bank report, he described the achievement as a result of collective efforts of society and citizens, with government welfare schemes also playing an important role.

The Prime Minister said the Centre has allocated more than ₹1 lakh crore for the PM-JANMAN scheme and the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan to accelerate development in the tribal areas that remained deprived of basic facilities.

The government has prioritised the deprived communities by providing more than four crore pucca houses to poor families, extending electricity to 18,000 villages that remained without power even decades after Independence, and providing free treatment of up to ₹5 lakh to people under the Ayushman Bharat scheme, the Prime Minister said.
More than 1.75 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs have been set up across the country, extending healthcare services to the remote tribal areas, he added.
The government, he noted, has also provided collateral-free loans under the MUDRA scheme to create livelihood opportunities for poor families.

articles.title: NIA arrests deported accused in Sri Lanka human trafficking case at Bengaluru airport
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: According to the NIA, Pudumadam Imran was actively involved in a conspiracy to traffic Sri Lankan nationals by promising to facilitate their migration to Canada using valid documents

The National Investigation Agency (NIA) on Friday (November 13, 2026) arrested Pudumadam Imran, an absconding accused in the Sri Lankan human trafficking case, after he was deported from Sri Lanka and handed over to Indian authorities.

Mr. Imran was detained by Sri Lankan authorities based on an Interpol Red Notice issued at the request of the NIA. Following his repatriation to India, an NIA team arrested him at Kempegowda International Airport in Bengaluru on November 13.
According to the NIA, Mr. Imran was actively involved in a conspiracy to traffic Sri Lankan nationals by promising to facilitate their migration to Canada using valid documents.
NIA nabs prime accused in Sri Lankan human trafficking case

He allegedly collected money from the victims’ family members and relatives and transferred the funds through hawala channels to co-accused persons in India to facilitate the trafficking and illegal confinement of the victims.
The case originated in 2021 when local police conducted raids at premises in Mangaluru based on credible information and found several Sri Lankan nationals staying there without valid documents.
A case was registered in this connection under Crime No. 103/2021, invoking various sections of the Indian Penal Code (IPC), the Foreigners Act and the Passport Act.

The NIA subsequently took over the investigation and re-registered the case in July 2021 under Sections 120B (criminal conspiracy), 370 (trafficking of persons) and 420 (cheating) of the IPC, Section 14 of the Foreigners Act and Section 12(1A) of the Passport Act.

Earlier, two other accused who were absconding in the case, Seeni Aabul Khan (A-9) and Imran Khan (A-7), were arrested in 2024 and 2025, respectively. Both are currently facing trial before the Special Court for NIA Cases in Bengaluru.

articles.title: Bomb threat emails target BMC, Pune civic body, PNB branches; searches find nothing suspicious
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: “A hoax bomb threat email was received at the BMC office and PNB Bank this morning. Nothing suspicious was found. Further legal process is ongoing,” Deputy Commissioner of Police (Zone 2) Raghasudha R. said

Bomb threat emails targeting civic offices in Mumbai and Pune, along with Punjab National Bank (PNB) branches in Mumbai, triggered security checks on Thursday (November 12, 2026). Police and bomb squad personnel searched the premises but found nothing suspicious.

According to police, threat emails were received at a Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) office and PNB branches in Zaveri Bazar and Marine Lines, claiming that explosives had been planted on the premises.
Local police and bomb detection and disposal squad personnel rushed to the locations and conducted searches following the alerts.

“A hoax bomb threat email was received at the BMC office and PNB Bank this morning. Nothing suspicious was found. Further legal process is ongoing,” Deputy Commissioner of Police (Zone 2) Raghasudha R. said.
The Mumbai Mayor’s office also received a bomb threat via email, prompting police and bomb squad personnel to reach the premises and initiate an investigation.

The threatening email also warned of explosions at multiple locations across Mumbai, including the airport and actor Amitabh Bachchan’s residence. According to sources, the email contained references to Khalistan and inflammatory remarks about the 1984 anti-Sikh violence.
Police are examining the technical trail of the emails, including the sender’s address and IP details, to trace their origin.

Meanwhile, the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) received a bomb threat on its official email address on Thursday. The sender claimed that an explosive device had been planted inside the civic body’s building and threatened to detonate it.
Fire brigade and bomb squad personnel rushed to the PMC premises and conducted a search. However, no suspicious objects were found.

articles.title: Congress government’s stricter implementation of eligibility saved expenditure on Rythu Bharosa: Study
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: There was nearly 45% drop in expenditure under the head in 2024-25 as compared to 2023-24

Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy-led Congress government has received appreciation for its stricter enforcement of eligibility criterion for extending benefits under Rythu Bharosa, the farmers’ investment support scheme.

An independent study has pointed out that stricter enforcement of eligibility criteria led to decline in expenditure from ₹13,576 crore in 2023-24 to ₹7,481 crore in 2024-25, a drop of 45%. The report “Public Finances of Telangana: Trends, Challenges and Policy Priorities”, released by the Centre for Economic and Social Studies, quoted the study as part of analysis of three major schemes — Rythu Bharosa, 24X7 free power and Aasara pensions — since the formation of Telangana.

Though these schemes routinely face issues of exclusion and inclusion errors, the success of meeting the objectives behind such schemes is conditional on the right targeting of beneficiaries. Rythu Bharosa (Rythu Bandhu during the previous Bharat Rashtra Samithi regime) was introduced in 2018-19 as a measure to provide income support to improve production and productivity. Under the Rythu Bandhu scheme, financial assistance was given to all landowners. However, the scheme has been misused and has excluded actual producers.

For instance, in a field study, it was found that major beneficiaries of the scheme were absentee landowners, whereas the tenants who were the actual cultivators did not benefit from the scheme. When the scheme did not have a ceiling on area or number of acres, it was the absentee landowners who owned the largest area received greater aid.

As per the study, the benefits received by the absentee landowners under the Rythu Bandhu was 20.5%. That is, the scheme benefitted the well-off and non-cultivators. “Schemes such as Rythu Bandhu are prone to misuse without right targeting,” the study said.

However, stricter enforcement of the eligibility criteria after the Congress government took over has ensured a significant decline in expenditure, despite increasing support from ₹5,000 to ₹6,000 per acre under Rythu Bharosa.

articles.title: Zelenskyy says Russia’s energy attacks helped by Starshield restrictions
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The Ukrainian President said Russia struck energy and railway infrastructure in eight regions overnight, with many strikes getting through because of limits on Starshield terminals

Russia struck energy and railway infrastructure in eight regions of Ukraine overnight, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Sunday (November 15, 2026), in attacks he said were made partly possible by restrictions on Ukraine’s use of SpaceX’s Starshield service.
“The Russians are targeting substations with ‘shaheds’,” he said on X, referring to the drones Russia commonly launches across Ukraine.
“And many of these strikes are getting through because restrictions on the operating speed of Starshield terminals along the front line and in the temporarily occupied territories are still there.”

articles.title: Guatemala declares state of emergency in east over drug violence
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The 30-day decree covers Zacapa and Izabal, a week after Congressman Julio Portillo and three police officers were killed in an armed attack

Guatemalan authorities declared a state of emergency on Saturday (November 14, 2026) in an area battered by violence linked to drug-trafficking groups, a week after a lawmaker was killed in an attack.
The decree, effective from Saturday for 30 days, restricts outdoor gatherings and bolsters powers for security forces in the eastern departments of Zacapa and Izabal.

Under the decree, security forces will be able to disperse groups by force, make arrests and enter residences without a warrant. The government said in a statement that the purpose of the decree was to “strengthen security” and “protect the population.”

Last week, Congressman Julio Portillo and three police officers were killed in an armed attack targeting the lawmaker in the town of Rio Hondo in Zacapa. The Lorenzana family cartel, which has ties to Mexico’s Sinaloa cartel, controls the drug trade in Zacapa.
The Lorenzanas were designated a terrorist organisation by the United States on Friday (November 13, 2026), along with the Mendoza family cartel, which has a strong presence in Izabal.

articles.title: Will discuss induction of woman Minister with high command: Karnataka CM
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The discussion on Cabinet expansion to fill the remaining two berths appears to be gaining traction again, especially with a little over a fortnight left for the commencement of the Winter Session of the legislature in Belagavi. The absence of a woman minister in the Cabinet has been a particular point of contention.

While the Cabinet headed by Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar was expanded in August, two Cabinet berths remain vacant, one following the resignation of B. Nagendra over charges of corruption, and another that has not been filled at all.

On Sunday, the Chief Minister said: “I have brought the matter of inducting a woman into the Cabinet to the attention of the Congress high command in Delhi. I cannot say whether the process will happen tomorrow, but they have told me that they will call me to Delhi to discuss it. This is something that needs to be done and we will definitely see it through.”

articles.title: Keralam government to hold talks with LPST protesters
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chief Minister’s Office informs protesters that the government is willing for talks as the agitation led by the All Kerala Lower Primary School Teachers (LPST) Rankholders’ Association enters its 133rd day

The Keralam government will hold talks with the representatives of the All Kerala Lower Primary School Teachers (LPST) Rankholders’ Association who have been on an agitation in front of the Secretariat for the past 133 days. The Chief Minister’s Office on Sunday informed the protesters that the government is willing for talks.
S. Valarmathi, the association secretary, who is on a fast-unto-death protest, said the agitation will be withdrawn only if the government agrees to the demands.

The LPST rank-holders began their protest over the delay in appointing candidates from the Kerala Public Service Commission (PSC) rank list to lower primary school teacher (LPST) posts, along with demands for changes to the teacher-recruitment system and teacher-student ratio.
The agitation, which began as a demand for appointment orders, has now expanded into a broader dispute over how teaching vacancies are calculated, reported and filled.

The LPST rank list came into effect in all 14 districts on May 31, 2025. The list reportedly has around 11,758 candidates, but fewer than 500 appointments had been made by August, according to reports.
